sentences.text: Pensioners on low incomes will be shielded from income tax by Chancellor John Healey in his first Budget on Wednesday.

sentences.text: The full, flat-rate state pension is expected to increase by 3.9% to £13,036.40 a year from April.
sentences.article_title: Healey to shield low-income pensioners from income tax in the Budget

sentences.text: This would take the payment above the £12,570 personal tax allowance and therefore be liable for income tax if no changes are made.
sentences.article_title: Healey to shield low-income pensioners from income tax in the Budget

sentences.text: The government had already committed to not taxing people who only get an income from the state pension.

sentences.text: Healey will explain this pledge will be met by plans for a new tax allowance for low-income pensioners.

sentences.text: Anthropic has warned artificial intelligence (AI) could pose "catastrophic or existential risks to humanity" as it unveiled details of its planned blockbuster stock market listing in the US.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic warns of 'catastrophic risk' to humankind ahead of blockbuster share listing

sentences.text: The firm's valuation is expected to exceed that of SpaceX, which was the biggest-ever stock listing at an initial valuation of about $1.8 trillion in the summer.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic warns of 'catastrophic risk' to humankind ahead of blockbuster share listing

sentences.text: Anthropic has not yet disclosed the number of shares to be released, their price range, and a date for the listing.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic warns of 'catastrophic risk' to humankind ahead of blockbuster share listing

sentences.text: The Claude chatbot developer revealed losses in a filing on Monday of more than $80.7bn (£60.5bn) in the first half of the year, but said it had $112.4bn in cash or equivalents, and generated revenues of $16.3bn over the same period.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic warns of 'catastrophic risk' to humankind ahead of blockbuster share listing

sentences.text: Anthropic will be the first true AI company to go public, making it a test case for the future of the technology.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic warns of 'catastrophic risk' to humankind ahead of blockbuster share listing

sentences.text: It said it will list on the Nasdaq under the symbol ANT.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic warns of 'catastrophic risk' to humankind ahead of blockbuster share listing

sentences.text: In a filing ahead of its listing, Anthropic said concerns had been raised by policymakers, regulators and researchers as well as by people within its organisation that AI systems posed a significant risk to humanity.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic warns of 'catastrophic risk' to humankind ahead of blockbuster share listing

sentences.text: It said advanced AI systems "could, if not developed, deployed, and operated with appropriate safeguards, oversight, and security measures, pose catastrophic or existential risks to humanity, particularly if such systems were misused, replicated, weaponised, or allowed to operate with a high degree of autonomy".
sentences.article_title: Anthropic warns of 'catastrophic risk' to humankind ahead of blockbuster share listing

sentences.text: Anthropic, which was founded just five years ago by chief executive Dario Amodei, his sister Daniela Amodei and five other co-founders, announced its intention to go public in June.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic warns of 'catastrophic risk' to humankind ahead of blockbuster share listing

sentences.text: Its most significant rival, OpenAI, quickly followed suit, saying it, too, intended to go public.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic warns of 'catastrophic risk' to humankind ahead of blockbuster share listing

sentences.text: That listing is now expected to occur early next year, according to a person familiar with OpenAI's plans.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic warns of 'catastrophic risk' to humankind ahead of blockbuster share listing

sentences.text: After the companies had decided on such plans, a wave of cyber-security and other types of technological breaches occurred involving their AI agents, or AI bots that are designed to operate somewhat autonomously.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic warns of 'catastrophic risk' to humankind ahead of blockbuster share listing

sentences.text: Current and former staff of both companies also gained public attention with new warnings that AI technology was being developed without the ability to protect the whole of humanity from possible future harms enacted by AI tools.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic warns of 'catastrophic risk' to humankind ahead of blockbuster share listing

sentences.text: As Anthropic revealed its stock debut plans on Monday, the owners of the rights to Elvis Presley's music sued the AI firm accusing it of using hundreds of the rock-and-roll star's songs to train its chatbot Claude.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic warns of 'catastrophic risk' to humankind ahead of blockbuster share listing

sentences.text: In Anthropic's new documents, it reiterated promises it has made in the past to develop AI in a way that is beneficial to people, while at the same time warning investors of its dangers.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic warns of 'catastrophic risk' to humankind ahead of blockbuster share listing

sentences.text: Anthropic detailed losses in its financial filings that exceeded its revenue for the first half of the year, but said it would often make forward investments "that may seem irresponsibly large at first glance".
sentences.article_title: Anthropic warns of 'catastrophic risk' to humankind ahead of blockbuster share listing

sentences.text: "In general, we will aim to be bold but sane, and to win trust with a track record of successful bets," the tech giant said.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic warns of 'catastrophic risk' to humankind ahead of blockbuster share listing

sentences.text: Its success depends largely on its ability to develop the most advanced AI models, Anthropic said, adding, "any failure to do so could adversely affect our business".
sentences.article_title: Anthropic warns of 'catastrophic risk' to humankind ahead of blockbuster share listing

sentences.text: Across about 90 pages detailing possible risk factors, Anthropic noted numerous potential threats to its ability to develop AI in a safe and competitive way.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic warns of 'catastrophic risk' to humankind ahead of blockbuster share listing

sentences.text: Highlighting potential issues, Anthropic cited its reliance on a cluster of cloud computing providers, Taiwanese chipmakers already facing huge demand, and data centres concentrated in the US.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic warns of 'catastrophic risk' to humankind ahead of blockbuster share listing

sentences.text: The filing also identified the potential for "regulatory action arising from harms associated with our AI models" – such as suicide and child safety – and uncertainty about where and how it might be held liable for actions taken by its systems.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic warns of 'catastrophic risk' to humankind ahead of blockbuster share listing

sentences.text: Tech companies have been heavily investing in costly AI infrastructure and tools, like data centres and the informational models that underly all AI technology, pouring more than $1tn into the efforts over the last year alone.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic warns of 'catastrophic risk' to humankind ahead of blockbuster share listing

sentences.text: Matt Orton, chief market strategist at investment management firm Raymond James Investment, said investors expected to see rapid growth as well as rapid financial losses in Anthropic's finances, so Monday's filing would not come as a surprise.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic warns of 'catastrophic risk' to humankind ahead of blockbuster share listing

sentences.text: "Getting the details from this filing, I think will help provide the market with more visibility, because we need to know where its revenue growth is coming from," he told the BBC.

sentences.text: Hardeep Bhachu and Jasskamal Riyat were sentenced at Leeds Crown Court Two men who killed a mother and her four-year-old daughter as they raced their high-performance cars along a Leeds city centre road have been jailed.
sentences.article_title: Drivers who killed mum and girl while racing jailed

sentences.text: Justyna Hulboj, 27, and her daughter Lena Czepczor were killed when they were hit by an Audi TT RS as they walked to the girl's nursery on the A61 Scott Hall Road on 16 January 2023.
sentences.article_title: Drivers who killed mum and girl while racing jailed

sentences.text: At Leeds Crown Court on Monday, Hardeep Bhachu, 29, was jailed for 12 years and Jasskamal Riyat, 37, for 16 years.
sentences.article_title: Drivers who killed mum and girl while racing jailed

sentences.text: Sentencing the men, Judge Singh said the road was "not a race track" and told them the deaths had consequences that were "immeasurable", with an "immense" impact on those left behind.
sentences.article_title: Drivers who killed mum and girl while racing jailed

sentences.text: Bhachu, of Grant Row in Adel, had earlier admitted two counts of causing death by dangerous driving , while Riyat, of Buckstone Avenue in Moortown, was convicted by a jury after denying he had been racing him.
sentences.article_title: Drivers who killed mum and girl while racing jailed

sentences.text: The court heard the pair, who did not previously know each other, accelerated away from traffic lights on Scott Hall Road shortly before the crash.
sentences.article_title: Drivers who killed mum and girl while racing jailed

sentences.text: Prosecutors said Riyat's BMW reached speeds of up to 89mph in the 40mph zone before Bhachu lost control of his Audi, mounted the pavement and struck Hulboj and her daughter.
sentences.article_title: Drivers who killed mum and girl while racing jailed

sentences.text: Justyna Hulboj, 27, and her four-year-old daughter Lena Czepczor were killed on Scott Hall Road in Leeds in January 2023 Judge Singh said the victims had "done nothing wrong" and were "simply walking to school".
sentences.article_title: Drivers who killed mum and girl while racing jailed

sentences.text: Addressing the defendants, he said: "A road is not a race track.
sentences.article_title: Drivers who killed mum and girl while racing jailed

sentences.text: A powerful car is not an invitation to test its limits on a public road.
sentences.article_title: Drivers who killed mum and girl while racing jailed

sentences.text: "The consequences of competitive driving at extreme speed can be, and in this case were, irreversible." He added: "Justyna and Lena should have gone to school that morning.
sentences.article_title: Drivers who killed mum and girl while racing jailed

sentences.text: They should have returned home.
sentences.article_title: Drivers who killed mum and girl while racing jailed

sentences.text: They should have continued with their lives.
sentences.article_title: Drivers who killed mum and girl while racing jailed

sentences.text: "Instead, their lives ended on a pavement because two drivers chose to drive in a manner which placed speed and competition above the safety of everyone around them." Susannah Proctor, for Bhachu, told the court that her client was a "normal person who's made a massive mistake".
sentences.article_title: Drivers who killed mum and girl while racing jailed

sentences.text: She said he "must live with himself in the knowledge of the devastation he has caused".
sentences.article_title: Drivers who killed mum and girl while racing jailed

sentences.text: And she said: "He did not intend to cause this devastation but cause it he has." Hulboj's fiancé Dominik Czepczor watched the sentencing hearing in court.
sentences.article_title: Drivers who killed mum and girl while racing jailed

sentences.text: A statement from him was read, which said: "My whole world collapsed in one second.
sentences.article_title: Drivers who killed mum and girl while racing jailed

sentences.text: "Every day I feel a huge void after their departure.
sentences.article_title: Drivers who killed mum and girl while racing jailed

sentences.text: "We had so many hopes and dreams and in one moment it all ended.
sentences.article_title: Drivers who killed mum and girl while racing jailed

sentences.text: "My dream was to have a wonderful family, and I must say that it came true for a short while, but that was taken away from me on January 16.
sentences.article_title: Drivers who killed mum and girl while racing jailed

sentences.text: "This sentencing hearing though does mark the end of a long criminal justice process for Justyna and Lena's family.
sentences.article_title: Drivers who killed mum and girl while racing jailed

sentences.text: "It is over two years since Bhachu admitted his part in this tragic incident and I know that the wait for justice has taken its toll.
sentences.article_title: Drivers who killed mum and girl while racing jailed

sentences.text: "My thoughts are firmly with them today." Listen to highlights from West Yorkshire on BBC Sounds , catch up with the latest episode of Look North .

sentences.text: Henry Nowak was 18 when he was stabbed to death in Southampton in December 2025 Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood has announced an independent review into the the murder of Henry Nowak.

sentences.text: The 18-year-old student was fatally stabbed in Southampton in December by Vickrum Digwa, who falsely claimed he had been racially abused and had acted in self-defence.
sentences.article_title: Independent review announced into murder of student Henry Nowak

sentences.text: Digwa was jailed for life on 1 June, with a minimum term of 21 years.
sentences.article_title: Independent review announced into murder of student Henry Nowak

sentences.text: Following the teenager's murder, police bodycam footage of him being handcuffed as he lay dying led to intense scrutiny of the Hampshire and Isle of Wight Constabulary and sparked wider debates around knife laws, race, policing and public trust.
sentences.article_title: Independent review announced into murder of student Henry Nowak

sentences.text: The review will be led by former Lord Chancellor Alex Chalk KC.
sentences.article_title: Independent review announced into murder of student Henry Nowak

sentences.text: "We must get to truth of what happened before, during and after that awful night and we must do everything in our power to ensure that no family suffers the same fate," Mahmood told the House of Commons on Monday.

sentences.text: Mahmood said the review will investigate what was known about Nowak's killer and if there were missed opportunities to intervene as well has how his family were treated in the aftermath.

sentences.text: Bern says her mother wanted to be cared for at home by her family A woman has described her "phenomenal" relief after she won a legal case that means she is entitled to be paid £127k from her mother's estate for caring for her in her final years.
sentences.article_title: Daughter wins £127k claim for caring for mum at home

sentences.text: Bern Rogers, from Bristol, told the BBC of the "harrowing and deeply sad" family dispute since her elderly mother Sheila died in 2020, which led to her facing criminal charges.
sentences.article_title: Daughter wins £127k claim for caring for mum at home

sentences.text: Legal experts said the "hugely significant" High Court ruling would lead to other claims.
sentences.article_title: Daughter wins £127k claim for caring for mum at home

sentences.text: The executor of Sheila's estate, Bern's brother Andrew, said it had "always been willing to pay" her "genuine expenses" and an extra amount for her efforts.
sentences.article_title: Daughter wins £127k claim for caring for mum at home

sentences.text: But the estate intends to appeal against the judgment that awarded Bern £127,500 for care provided.
sentences.article_title: Daughter wins £127k claim for caring for mum at home

sentences.text: Theatres at risk and fighting back across the West 'Beloved cats need more protection from drivers' Teenage boy dies in crash following police pursuit Bern looked after Sheila, who had dementia, for two-and-a-half years.
sentences.article_title: Daughter wins £127k claim for caring for mum at home

sentences.text: After Sheila moved into Bern's house in Bristol in September 2017, she wanted to be cared for by her daughter rather than get costly home care or go into a residential care home.
sentences.article_title: Daughter wins £127k claim for caring for mum at home

sentences.text: Crucially, Bern said she agreed with her mother she would be paid for the round-the-clock care.
sentences.article_title: Daughter wins £127k claim for caring for mum at home

sentences.text: After Sheila died in April 2020, Bern took £100,000 from her estate.
sentences.article_title: Daughter wins £127k claim for caring for mum at home

sentences.text: It led to her being reported to the police for fraud and theft.
sentences.article_title: Daughter wins £127k claim for caring for mum at home

sentences.text: The money was seized and Bern was charged.
sentences.article_title: Daughter wins £127k claim for caring for mum at home

sentences.text: But, at a trial at Bristol Crown Court in 2022, she was found not guilty by a jury.
sentences.article_title: Daughter wins £127k claim for caring for mum at home

sentences.text: After being cleared, Bern turned to the civil courts.
sentences.article_title: Daughter wins £127k claim for caring for mum at home

sentences.text: In 2025, a High Court judge ruled she had entered into an informal contract with Sheila for payment of a reasonable sum for her care.
sentences.article_title: Daughter wins £127k claim for caring for mum at home

sentences.text: The estate was also ordered by a judge to pay Bern's legal costs.
sentences.article_title: Daughter wins £127k claim for caring for mum at home

sentences.text: In August this year, another High Court judge worked out the amount Bern was due and ruled she was owed £127,500 for the 850 days of care she provided.
sentences.article_title: Daughter wins £127k claim for caring for mum at home

sentences.text: Sheila was diagnosed with dementia after moving in with her daughter "Mum came to live with me, she became very confused and was seen wandering in the garden and obviously needed care," Bern said.
sentences.article_title: Daughter wins £127k claim for caring for mum at home

sentences.text: "We didn't know what was wrong with her." She said caring for her mother had been like a full-time job, adding: "I couldn't leave her really.
sentences.article_title: Daughter wins £127k claim for caring for mum at home

sentences.text: She became unpredictable." Sheila became more frail, was diagnosed with dementia and also had a series of physical health problems, including a "chronic" and "disabling" prolapse.
sentences.article_title: Daughter wins £127k claim for caring for mum at home

sentences.text: Bern's husband Jon said: "It was relentless after she moved in with us.
sentences.article_title: Daughter wins £127k claim for caring for mum at home

sentences.text: We couldn't go out even to the shops.
sentences.article_title: Daughter wins £127k claim for caring for mum at home

sentences.text: "It was a privilege, but we had to put our lives on hold for more than two years and revolve our lives around looking after her." He remembered that in Sheila's final weeks, his wife was sleeping on the floor of her mother's bedroom to make sure she was alright.
sentences.article_title: Daughter wins £127k claim for caring for mum at home

sentences.text: Bern said "of course" she would have looked after her mother if she had not been able to pay her.
sentences.article_title: Daughter wins £127k claim for caring for mum at home

sentences.text: But she said her mother had wanted to be looked after by her daughter rather than getting professional carers or going into a home, which would have cost thousands of pounds a month.
sentences.article_title: Daughter wins £127k claim for caring for mum at home

sentences.text: "She was very insistent and would tell anyone that would listen that she wanted to make sure that I sorted out money for her care, I was to make sure I got paid properly," she said.
sentences.article_title: Daughter wins £127k claim for caring for mum at home

sentences.text: Multiple messages from Bern's five siblings were shown in court saying that she should be paid something for the care, although no amount was agreed.
sentences.article_title: Daughter wins £127k claim for caring for mum at home

sentences.text: That is why, she explained, shortly after her mother had died, she transferred £100,000 from her mother's account.
sentences.article_title: Daughter wins £127k claim for caring for mum at home

sentences.text: Bern was reported to the police for theft and fraud, which she describes as a "terrible and devastating betrayal".
sentences.article_title: Daughter wins £127k claim for caring for mum at home

sentences.text: "It has been harrowing and deeply sad for it to go from a normal family relationship to being treated like a scapegoat, five against one," she said.
sentences.article_title: Daughter wins £127k claim for caring for mum at home

sentences.text: Bern Rogers says she and her husband Jon can get on with their lives now after the two High Court rulings After the two separate High Court judgements in her favour, Bern said: "The weight off my shoulders was phenomenal.
sentences.article_title: Daughter wins £127k claim for caring for mum at home

sentences.text: "It has been absolutely wonderful to be vindicated.
sentences.article_title: Daughter wins £127k claim for caring for mum at home

sentences.text: It means I can get on with my life now, the rest of my retirement." Jon said: "I'm very proud of her, actually, because she has stuck up for her mother, for carers and for herself.
sentences.article_title: Daughter wins £127k claim for caring for mum at home

sentences.text: "It's been a very long and tough journey of nine years, and we've finally got justice." Legal experts have told the BBC that while this case does not automatically set a legal precedent, it is likely to lead to similar claims in future.
sentences.article_title: Daughter wins £127k claim for caring for mum at home

sentences.text: "These are considered, well-reasoned judgements by highly esteemed judges, so I would think it's very likely that future courts will follow them," Holland said.
sentences.article_title: Daughter wins £127k claim for caring for mum at home

sentences.text: Beth Middleton, senior associate in private wealth and disputes at JMW, said this was a "hugely significant" case that would "open a floodgate of claims".
sentences.article_title: Daughter wins £127k claim for caring for mum at home

sentences.text: Samara Dutton, partner at Collyer Bristow, who specialises in trusts, inheritance and wills, said the judgements were likely to be "influential".
sentences.article_title: Daughter wins £127k claim for caring for mum at home

sentences.text: "It demonstrates a willingness to look beyond individual care tasks and acknowledges the broader reality of providing care to an elderly relative, including the continuous supervision, responsibility and restrictions on personal freedom," she said.
sentences.article_title: Daughter wins £127k claim for caring for mum at home

sentences.text: Bern Rogers and her husband Jon say they feel pride that their ordeal could help other family carers in future Bern said she was "terribly proud" that her case could influence others in future, which she said was her mum's "legacy".
sentences.article_title: Daughter wins £127k claim for caring for mum at home

sentences.text: "It's a huge win for carers everywhere," Jon added, but stressed families still needed to have open discussions about what was fair.
sentences.article_title: Daughter wins £127k claim for caring for mum at home

sentences.text: The ruling that states that Bern is entitled to payment cannot be appealed against, however, the estate intends to lodge an appeal against the second ruling that decided the amount owed.
sentences.article_title: Daughter wins £127k claim for caring for mum at home

sentences.text: The executor of Sheila's estate is Bern's brother, Andrew Wills.
sentences.article_title: Daughter wins £127k claim for caring for mum at home

sentences.text: In a statement on behalf of the estate, he said: "The only agreements that we (her siblings) were aware of was for my mother to give Bernadette £50 per week 'keep' and to ensure that Bernadette was not to be out of pocket.
sentences.article_title: Daughter wins £127k claim for caring for mum at home

sentences.text: "We were not made aware of any other contract between our mother and Bernadette." The statement added: "At all times I have attempted to be independent and to act in the best interests of the estate.
sentences.article_title: Daughter wins £127k claim for caring for mum at home

sentences.text: "The estate has always been willing to pay Bernadette her genuine expenses as well as an additional gratuity in recognition of her efforts for our mother.
sentences.article_title: Daughter wins £127k claim for caring for mum at home

sentences.text: "We have always tried to be fair.
sentences.article_title: Daughter wins £127k claim for caring for mum at home

sentences.text: Unfortunately, our offers were not accepted by Bernadette who instead issued legal proceedings against the estate." Follow BBC Bristol on Facebook , external , X , external and Instagram , external .
sentences.article_title: Daughter wins £127k claim for caring for mum at home

sentences.text: Around 90,000 properties are still without power as parts of Scotland and north England were battered by Storm Boelo over the weekend.
sentences.article_title: Storm Boelo leaves 90,000 without power as Met Office issues new wind warning

sentences.text: A clean-up operation is under way in parts of the UK after Storm Boelo caused flooding and property damage, leaving thousands without power.
sentences.article_title: Storm Boelo leaves 90,000 without power as Met Office issues new wind warning

sentences.text: The Energy Networks Association (ENA) said around 90,000 properties are still without power as of Monday.
sentences.article_title: Storm Boelo leaves 90,000 without power as Met Office issues new wind warning

sentences.text: Two men were killed by falling trees during the storm on Sunday - a man in his 20s whose car was hit in north London and a 60-year-old in Mid Kelton, Dumfries and Galloway.
sentences.article_title: Storm Boelo leaves 90,000 without power as Met Office issues new wind warning

sentences.text: The Met Office has issued a yellow warning for strong winds from 18:00 on Monday to 03:00 on Tuesday across the west coast of England, Wales and Scotland and eastern parts of Northern Ireland.
sentences.article_title: Storm Boelo leaves 90,000 without power as Met Office issues new wind warning

sentences.text: The Met Office has warned that further power cuts in areas covered by the warning are likely and people should make sure they have essentials prepared, including torches and batteries.
sentences.article_title: Storm Boelo leaves 90,000 without power as Met Office issues new wind warning

sentences.text: Coastal communities could also be affected by spray or large waves, while travel delays are expected.
sentences.article_title: Storm Boelo leaves 90,000 without power as Met Office issues new wind warning

sentences.text: Boelo is the second storm to have hit parts of the UK in recent days, following Storm Austen.
sentences.article_title: Storm Boelo leaves 90,000 without power as Met Office issues new wind warning

sentences.text: Leo Slade, CEO of the ENA said it had been "a tough weekend" and that efforts to reconnect some properties were being hampered by the weather, with sustained winds of 50-85mph across parts of Scotland and northern England.
sentences.article_title: Storm Boelo leaves 90,000 without power as Met Office issues new wind warning

sentences.text: "Until that weather system passes, we can't safely get engineers out to replace poles, to get wires back up, so today is going to be a hive of activity in getting engineers out into the field," Slade told BBC Radio 4's Today programme.
sentences.article_title: Storm Boelo leaves 90,000 without power as Met Office issues new wind warning

sentences.text: He stressed that the UK's power network was very resilient and money was spent to prepare for these sorts of scenarios, but said a debate was needed over how much more investment was required to mitigate for further storms brought by climate change.
sentences.article_title: Storm Boelo leaves 90,000 without power as Met Office issues new wind warning

sentences.text: Storm Boelo clears but more wind and rain bears down on UK Marcus Reed, the operations director at a home fragrance manufacturer, said his factory and shop in Lyndal, Cumbria would be without power until Tuesday evening.
sentences.article_title: Storm Boelo leaves 90,000 without power as Met Office issues new wind warning

sentences.text: He told the Today programme that he has had to turn away employees and customers.
sentences.article_title: Storm Boelo leaves 90,000 without power as Met Office issues new wind warning

sentences.text: "To lose two days manufacturing and distribution is going to be really disruptive," he said, adding that it was bad timing as it was "the busiest time of the year" for his business in the lead-up to Christmas.
sentences.article_title: Storm Boelo leaves 90,000 without power as Met Office issues new wind warning

sentences.text: "This is probably the worst situation I've experienced in my time here; we've had ad hoc issues over weekends where we've lost power, but it's been contained within a 12-hour period.
sentences.article_title: Storm Boelo leaves 90,000 without power as Met Office issues new wind warning

sentences.text: It's the first time anything like this has happened, it's very serious." Wendy McKinney, whose bathroom shop in the seaside town of Largs in North Ayrshire was flooded on Sunday, told the Today programme the storm had been "devastating to local businesses".
sentences.article_title: Storm Boelo leaves 90,000 without power as Met Office issues new wind warning

sentences.text: A spokesperson said council teams "followed established resilience procedures" but would review flooding reports and "consider any lessons that can be learned".
sentences.article_title: Storm Boelo leaves 90,000 without power as Met Office issues new wind warning

sentences.article_title: Storm Boelo leaves 90,000 without power as Met Office issues new wind warning

sentences.text: Monday morning has seen rain in many parts of south-west England, Wales and Northern Ireland, and this is moving north-eastwards reaching central, eastern and northern England, as well as most of Scotland, by around lunchtime.
sentences.article_title: Storm Boelo leaves 90,000 without power as Met Office issues new wind warning

sentences.text: Winds will also strengthen throughout Monday, and it will turn even windier overnight as the area of low pressure passes close to Northern Ireland and north-west Scotland with gusts peaking on Tuesday.

sentences.text: This video can not be played Watch: Chris Brown greeted with cheers as he leaves court US singer Chris Brown has avoided jail after striking a man twice in the head with a glass tequila bottle in a London nightclub.
sentences.article_title: Chris Brown given suspended eight-month prison sentence over nightclub attack

sentences.text: The R&B star was given an eight-month prison sentence, suspended for 12 months, over the attack at private members' club Tape in Mayfair, in the early hours of 19 February 2023.
sentences.article_title: Chris Brown given suspended eight-month prison sentence over nightclub attack

sentences.text: Brown's vocal coach, rapper Omololu Akinlolu, who joined the attack, was sentenced to four months' imprisonment, suspended for 12 months.
sentences.article_title: Chris Brown given suspended eight-month prison sentence over nightclub attack

sentences.text: Both men, who had pleaded guilty to affray, were also ordered to pay £1,500 costs.
sentences.article_title: Chris Brown given suspended eight-month prison sentence over nightclub attack

sentences.text: Judge Tony Baumgartner said Brown's use of the glass bottle to hit the victim twice over the head "was plainly dangerous", adding that the violence of the attack was "intense".
sentences.article_title: Chris Brown given suspended eight-month prison sentence over nightclub attack

sentences.text: This video can not be played Met Police release annotated CCTV footage of Chris Brown's 2023 nightclub attack The sentence means Brown will not be imprisoned unless he commits another offence during the 12-month period of suspension.
sentences.article_title: Chris Brown given suspended eight-month prison sentence over nightclub attack

sentences.text: The court heard Brown's attack on music producer Abraham 'Abe' Diaw left the victim in need of hospital treatment for his injuries.
sentences.article_title: Chris Brown given suspended eight-month prison sentence over nightclub attack

sentences.text: Sentencing Brown, Judge Baumgartner said: "This was not planned violence.
sentences.article_title: Chris Brown given suspended eight-month prison sentence over nightclub attack

sentences.text: The judge said Brown's fame, commercial success and professional standing "do not entitle you to special treatment - the law applies equally to everyone".
sentences.article_title: Chris Brown given suspended eight-month prison sentence over nightclub attack

sentences.text: But judge Baumgartner also said he had noted Brown's guilty plea, compliance with bail conditions, and the impact a custodial sentence would have on Brown's children, and said the singer's "risk of further offending is low".
sentences.article_title: Chris Brown given suspended eight-month prison sentence over nightclub attack

sentences.text: Brown and Akinlolu pleaded guilty to a charge of affray at Southwark Crown Court in July.
sentences.article_title: Chris Brown given suspended eight-month prison sentence over nightclub attack

sentences.text: The singer had been due to face a trial on more serious charges, which he denied, and which were subsequently dropped.
sentences.article_title: Chris Brown given suspended eight-month prison sentence over nightclub attack

sentences.text: These were assault, attempting to cause grievous bodily harm, and having an offensive weapon.
sentences.article_title: Chris Brown given suspended eight-month prison sentence over nightclub attack

sentences.text: Following Brown and Akinlolu's guilty pleas, the CPS released a statement outlining that Brown had approached Diaw on the dance floor, hitting him over the head with a glass bottle twice, before Akinlolu then punched Diaw in the head.
sentences.article_title: Chris Brown given suspended eight-month prison sentence over nightclub attack

sentences.text: "They continued their assault whilst the victim attempted to flee through the club," the CPS said.
sentences.article_title: Chris Brown given suspended eight-month prison sentence over nightclub attack

sentences.text: "The victim was kicked while he was seated defenceless on the floor." Judge Baumgartner told the pair that while he had concluded they had both crossed the threshold to be jailed, this year's changes to sentencing laws meant that he had to put off doing so, unless there were exceptional reasons.
sentences.article_title: Chris Brown given suspended eight-month prison sentence over nightclub attack

sentences.text: "I have considered whether the seriousness of the offending, taken together with the need for punishment and deterrence, amounts to exceptional circumstances requiring immediate imprisonment.
sentences.article_title: Chris Brown given suspended eight-month prison sentence over nightclub attack

sentences.text: I have concluded, in relation to each of you, that it does not," he said.
sentences.article_title: Chris Brown given suspended eight-month prison sentence over nightclub attack

sentences.text: The attack lasted no more than 20 seconds, but Brown could be seen hitting the victim four times with a tequila bottle, twice to the head.
sentences.article_title: Chris Brown given suspended eight-month prison sentence over nightclub attack

sentences.text: Prosecutor, Heidi Stonecliffe KC, described the weapon as a "heavy square-shaped tequila bottle" and said Diaw was approached by Brown at around 03:00.
sentences.article_title: Chris Brown given suspended eight-month prison sentence over nightclub attack

sentences.text: The footage showed that the nightclub was very small and packed at the time.
sentences.article_title: Chris Brown given suspended eight-month prison sentence over nightclub attack

sentences.text: The defence described Chris Brown as a "dedicated and a loving father of four children," someone who is "positive and present".
sentences.article_title: Chris Brown given suspended eight-month prison sentence over nightclub attack

sentences.text: Consultant doctors in England are to stage a two-day strike next month in a dispute over pay and working conditions.

sentences.text: The walkout will begin on 25 November at 06:59 GMT, with consultants staffing emergency care only.
sentences.article_title: Consultant doctors in England to strike next month

sentences.text: This is known as Christmas Day cover and is likely to have a major impact on most routine and elective or planned services.
sentences.article_title: Consultant doctors in England to strike next month

sentences.text: The announcement comes after talks had been taking place with the government over the past month, following the vote in favour of strike action by British Medical Association members in July.
sentences.article_title: Consultant doctors in England to strike next month

sentences.text: Consultants – the most senior doctors in hospitals – were given a 3.5% pay increase this year.
sentences.article_title: Consultant doctors in England to strike next month

sentences.text: But the BMA argues pay has fallen by a quarter over the past 17 years, once inflation is taken into account.
sentences.article_title: Consultant doctors in England to strike next month

sentences.text: The union also wants a reduction in the standard working week, from 40 to 35 hours, and higher pay for out-of-hours work, alongside changes to pensions, including greater flexibility over when they can be taken.
sentences.article_title: Consultant doctors in England to strike next month

sentences.text: In a joint statement, BMA consultants committee co-chairs Dr Helen Neary and Dr Shanu Datta, said they had tried to negotiate with the government in "good faith", but "time-and-time again ministers have kicked the can down the road".
sentences.article_title: Consultant doctors in England to strike next month

sentences.text: "Unfortunately, that road has now run out, and we have been forced to announce strikes.
sentences.article_title: Consultant doctors in England to strike next month

sentences.text: "Consultants take their responsibilities incredibly seriously, and striking does not come naturally, but we are hearing loud and clear from the profession that they have had enough." Average earnings for consultants top £150,000 a year.
sentences.article_title: Consultant doctors in England to strike next month

sentences.text: Basic pay starts at £113,500, with the most experienced getting £150,500.
sentences.article_title: Consultant doctors in England to strike next month

sentences.text: But many earn tens of thousands in extra payments and awards.
sentences.article_title: Consultant doctors in England to strike next month

sentences.text: In the strike ballot, 76% of consultants who took part voted in favour of strike action, with just over half of eligible BMA members taking part.
sentences.article_title: Consultant doctors in England to strike next month

sentences.text: The government says this represents only around one in five consultants employed by the NHS in England voting for strike action, as nearly half are not BMA members.
sentences.article_title: Consultant doctors in England to strike next month

sentences.text: Health Secretary Yvette Cooper said the government had been in "constructive discussions" with the BMA so it was "disappointing" the strike dates had been announced.
sentences.article_title: Consultant doctors in England to strike next month

sentences.text: The prime minister has left the door open to a potential referendum on freedom of movement with the European Union.
sentences.article_title: Burnham leaves door open to referendum on EU free movement

sentences.text: Asked by broadcasters if he could introduce free movement without a referendum, Andy Burnham said "no", but sources told the BBC no decision on that has been made.
sentences.article_title: Burnham leaves door open to referendum on EU free movement

sentences.text: The PM added that he would "never move ahead of the British public when it comes to Brexit".
sentences.article_title: Burnham leaves door open to referendum on EU free movement

sentences.text: Burnham has ruled out major changes to the UK's relationship with the EU before the next general election but says he wants start a conversation about potential options, with these expected to be set out around the time of the EU summit next month.
sentences.article_title: Burnham leaves door open to referendum on EU free movement

sentences.text: Freedom of movement, which allows EU citizens to travel, live, study and work in any member country, is a precondition of membership of the EU's single market.
sentences.article_title: Burnham leaves door open to referendum on EU free movement

sentences.text: The single market enables goods, services and people to move freely between member states, with countries also applying many common rules and standards.
sentences.article_title: Burnham leaves door open to referendum on EU free movement

sentences.text: The prime minister is thought to be against the idea of leaping quickly to a return to freedom of movement.
sentences.article_title: Burnham leaves door open to referendum on EU free movement

sentences.text: Sources indicated no firm decision had been made on whether free movement would need to be rubber-stamped by a referendum.
sentences.article_title: Burnham leaves door open to referendum on EU free movement

sentences.text: Burnham is said to believe that a conversation about the UK's future relationship with Brussels needs to happen first.
sentences.article_title: Burnham leaves door open to referendum on EU free movement

sentences.text: Migration dominated debate during the 2016 Brexit campaign, with the Leave campaign raising issues about freedom of movement allowing any EU citizen to move to the UK.
sentences.article_title: Burnham leaves door open to referendum on EU free movement

sentences.text: Burnham open to 'honest discussion' on EU free movement Brexit referendum 'possible' in Labour election manifesto, says Burnham Burnham has said he is committed to Labour's 2024 election manifesto, which ruled out a return of free movement, single market membership or a customs union.
sentences.article_title: Burnham leaves door open to referendum on EU free movement

sentences.text: The PM has stressed any changes would require a mandate at a general election, which is due by 2029.
sentences.article_title: Burnham leaves door open to referendum on EU free movement

sentences.text: However, he has suggested potential options for the future could range from no changes to the UK-EU relationship, to rejoining the EU customs union, the single market or a new in-out referendum on full EU membership.
sentences.article_title: Burnham leaves door open to referendum on EU free movement

sentences.text: In an interview with the Sunday Times , external , Burnham said he would welcome an "honest discussion" about the prospect of returning to free movement between the UK and the EU.
sentences.article_title: Burnham leaves door open to referendum on EU free movement

sentences.text: The PM argued that the type of migration had changed since Brexit, with more foreigners moving permanently.
sentences.article_title: Burnham leaves door open to referendum on EU free movement

sentences.text: In contrast, he suggested that when the UK was a member of the EU, migration was "generally younger people", who would spend a few years in the country before returning home.
sentences.article_title: Burnham leaves door open to referendum on EU free movement

sentences.text: However, Burnham added: "I can't see myself ever recommending anything that would involve joining the euro or Schengen." The Schengen Agreement, which the UK was not part of when it was in the EU, allows passport-free travel across member countries.
sentences.article_title: Burnham leaves door open to referendum on EU free movement

sentences.text: The UK was able to keep the pound when it was an EU member, but the bloc has pushed new members to adopt the Euro.
sentences.article_title: Burnham leaves door open to referendum on EU free movement

sentences.text: Burnham has argued that since Brexit, the UK has lost immigration control the country previously had.
sentences.article_title: Burnham leaves door open to referendum on EU free movement

sentences.text: "For instance, the small boats crisis has arisen in the last 10 years because we lost that returns agreement when people came here that we could work with other countries to return them," he told broadcasters.
sentences.article_title: Burnham leaves door open to referendum on EU free movement

sentences.text: The Conservatives and Reform UK both oppose a return to free movement with the EU.
sentences.article_title: Burnham leaves door open to referendum on EU free movement

sentences.text: Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch argued most people who voted for Brexit did so because they did not want free movement, while Reform leader Nigel Farage said such a move would be "a total betrayal of Brexit Britain".
sentences.article_title: Burnham leaves door open to referendum on EU free movement

sentences.text: However, the Liberal Democrats have argued that allowing freedom of movement would help economic growth.

sentences.text: Healey's Budget needs to sustain the stronger economy through gathering clouds There have been almost no Budget leaks.

sentences.text: The IT has been locked down and ministers viewing the plans have to sign a digital promise not to brief media.
sentences.article_title: Faisal Islam: Healey's Budget needs to sustain the stronger economy through gathering clouds

sentences.article_title: Faisal Islam: Healey's Budget needs to sustain the stronger economy through gathering clouds

sentences.text: As a recent former defence secretary, Chancellor John Healey has embraced such strict procedures, and has approached most of his public engagements and interviews with a sturdy refusal to break the Budget omertà, akin to his fellow Yorkshireman Geoffrey Boycott's at times ultra-defensive stance on a cricket pitch.
sentences.article_title: Faisal Islam: Healey's Budget needs to sustain the stronger economy through gathering clouds

sentences.text: The economic news has been good - growth has been better than expected and the International Monetary Fund has endorsed the UK for "standing out" among the G7 countries for at least planning to cut borrowing.

sentences.text: Big, noisy and coming to a town near you - why the data centre backlash is growing Until a few years ago many of us may have been blissfully unaware of what a data centre was.
sentences.article_title: Big, noisy and coming to a town near you - why the data centre backlash is growing

sentences.text: These giant, warehouse-like buildings power virtually all our internet activity, from our web searches and emails to movie downloads and online banking.
sentences.article_title: Big, noisy and coming to a town near you - why the data centre backlash is growing

sentences.text: They are at the heart of the AI boom, housing the advanced computer chips and servers needed to run services like ChatGPT and Claude.
sentences.article_title: Big, noisy and coming to a town near you - why the data centre backlash is growing

sentences.text: But the speed at which they're growing, the enormous amount of electricity they consume and concerns about their environmental impact are fuelling a public backlash around the world.
sentences.article_title: Big, noisy and coming to a town near you - why the data centre backlash is growing

sentences.text: In the US, they've become a huge issue ahead of the midterm elections on 3 November, with both Republicans and opposition Democrats coming out against their development.
sentences.article_title: Big, noisy and coming to a town near you - why the data centre backlash is growing

sentences.text: It's putting opponents of data centre expansion on a collision course with US President Donald Trump, who has dismissed the pushback as a "sick conspiracy", even as public anger grows.
sentences.article_title: Big, noisy and coming to a town near you - why the data centre backlash is growing

sentences.text: Here's what you need to know about the data centre boom, and why opposition is growing.
sentences.article_title: Big, noisy and coming to a town near you - why the data centre backlash is growing

sentences.text: There are about 12,250 data centres around the world, according to Data Center Map , external , a company that tracks both operational and pre-operational sites.
sentences.article_title: Big, noisy and coming to a town near you - why the data centre backlash is growing

sentences.text: That's up sharply from 2021, when there were around 8,000 , external operational sites.
sentences.article_title: Big, noisy and coming to a town near you - why the data centre backlash is growing

sentences.text: As the chart below shows, data centres are most densely clustered in the US which has 4,767 sites.
sentences.article_title: Big, noisy and coming to a town near you - why the data centre backlash is growing

sentences.text: It is followed by Europe, where the UK and Germany lead.
sentences.article_title: Big, noisy and coming to a town near you - why the data centre backlash is growing

sentences.text: Data centres have typically been located near to cities where it's easier to access high voltage power lines or water resources for cooling.
sentences.article_title: Big, noisy and coming to a town near you - why the data centre backlash is growing

sentences.text: But as they get bigger, more are being built in rural areas.
sentences.article_title: Big, noisy and coming to a town near you - why the data centre backlash is growing

sentences.text: But when it comes to actual capacity, the US is ahead by a much larger margin, with China in second place and Europe lagging far behind.
sentences.article_title: Big, noisy and coming to a town near you - why the data centre backlash is growing

sentences.text: This gap is set to widen in the coming years, leading some to warn Europe risks missing out on the potential economic benefits of the AI boom , external .
sentences.article_title: Big, noisy and coming to a town near you - why the data centre backlash is growing

sentences.text: Data centres vary wildly in size, ranging from ones that fit inside a garden shed to others covering vast expanses of land.
sentences.article_title: Big, noisy and coming to a town near you - why the data centre backlash is growing

sentences.text: The world's largest operational data centre is widely reported to be one run by China Telecom in Hohhot, Inner Mongolia, covering an area of approximately one million square metres (10.7 million sq ft).
sentences.article_title: Big, noisy and coming to a town near you - why the data centre backlash is growing

sentences.text: That is equivalent to about 140 Fifa football pitches.
sentences.article_title: Big, noisy and coming to a town near you - why the data centre backlash is growing

sentences.text: However, much larger sites are under construction as the graphic below shows.
sentences.article_title: Big, noisy and coming to a town near you - why the data centre backlash is growing

sentences.text: All these sites are being built exclusively to provide the immense computing power needed to run AI services.
sentences.article_title: Big, noisy and coming to a town near you - why the data centre backlash is growing

sentences.text: For instance, Colossus 2, which is part of the wider Colossus campus, will house hundreds of thousands of advanced AI chips made by tech giant Nvidia.
sentences.article_title: Big, noisy and coming to a town near you - why the data centre backlash is growing

sentences.text: It will also be used to train xAI's chatbot Grok.
sentences.article_title: Big, noisy and coming to a town near you - why the data centre backlash is growing

sentences.text: Elon Musk's company will use 41 methane gas turbines to help power the site, which activists say could "significantly increase" local air pollution , external .
sentences.article_title: Big, noisy and coming to a town near you - why the data centre backlash is growing

sentences.text: Local regulators say the turbines will meet air quality standards.
sentences.article_title: Big, noisy and coming to a town near you - why the data centre backlash is growing

sentences.text: The pressure data centres put on local resources has sparked increasing concern.
sentences.article_title: Big, noisy and coming to a town near you - why the data centre backlash is growing

sentences.text: These facilities can use significant amounts of water to cool their systems, which could lead to water shortages , some experts say.
sentences.article_title: Big, noisy and coming to a town near you - why the data centre backlash is growing

sentences.text: Data centres worldwide are also thought to consume more electricity than the whole of France, as the chart below shows.
sentences.article_title: Big, noisy and coming to a town near you - why the data centre backlash is growing

sentences.text: This growing hunger for power is driving up carbon emissions, analysis shows , while putting pressure on local grids, which some fear could push up energy prices .
sentences.article_title: Big, noisy and coming to a town near you - why the data centre backlash is growing

sentences.text: With others worried about the noise data centres make and the space they take up, a public backlash is gathering steam.
sentences.article_title: Big, noisy and coming to a town near you - why the data centre backlash is growing

sentences.text: Some 16 US states have proposed laws to ban or temporarily block new facilities, and it could be a key issue in November's midterm elections .
sentences.article_title: Big, noisy and coming to a town near you - why the data centre backlash is growing

sentences.text: Outside the US, opposition to data centres has emerged in countries like Mexico , France, Indonesia and the UK .
sentences.article_title: Big, noisy and coming to a town near you - why the data centre backlash is growing

sentences.text: But supporters say data centres are critical to national security , and the development of AI.
sentences.article_title: Big, noisy and coming to a town near you - why the data centre backlash is growing

sentences.text: They also say they are good for the economy , external , attracting investment, generating tax revenue and creating jobs in areas like construction.
sentences.article_title: Big, noisy and coming to a town near you - why the data centre backlash is growing

sentences.text: A recent report by the Brookings Center , external suggests data centres do create local jobs, although fewer than industry advocates claim.
sentences.article_title: Big, noisy and coming to a town near you - why the data centre backlash is growing

sentences.text: The type of data centre matters too.
sentences.article_title: Big, noisy and coming to a town near you - why the data centre backlash is growing

sentences.text: So-called hyperscale facilities - massive sites owned and run by tech giants like Amazon and Microsoft - have a bigger positive effect on jobs, it found.
sentences.article_title: Big, noisy and coming to a town near you - why the data centre backlash is growing

sentences.text: But "colocation" facilities, which lease space to remote tenants without a local presence, brought fewer benefits.
sentences.article_title: Big, noisy and coming to a town near you - why the data centre backlash is growing

sentences.text: As the debate over their merits intensifies, the data centre rollout continues.
sentences.article_title: Big, noisy and coming to a town near you - why the data centre backlash is growing

sentences.text: This year, the tech industry is expected to spend a combined $765bn , external ($544bn) on AI infrastructure in 2026, with this topping $1tn next year.
sentences.article_title: Big, noisy and coming to a town near you - why the data centre backlash is growing

sentences.text: But as concerns about the environmental impact grow, the tech industry is exploring alternatives.
sentences.article_title: Big, noisy and coming to a town near you - why the data centre backlash is growing

sentences.text: One idea is to put data centres in space , external or on the Moon , where they could harness abundant solar energy.
sentences.article_title: Big, noisy and coming to a town near you - why the data centre backlash is growing

sentences.text: Others predict that more AI processing could eventually be carried out by the hardware already inside our computers and smartphones , reducing the need for vast data centres altogether.
sentences.article_title: Big, noisy and coming to a town near you - why the data centre backlash is growing

sentences.text: Devin Jacob Ballard was stationed at Futenma Air Station A US Marine has been indicted on suspicion of murdering and robbing a woman in Japan earlier this month in a case that has triggered protests, Japanese media reports.
sentences.article_title: US Marine indicted for murder and robbery of woman in Japan

sentences.text: Devin Jacob Ballard, 20, who was stationed at US Marine Corps Air Station Futenma, was arrested on suspicion of killing Anna Yagi, 39, at a hotel in Naha, the capital of Okinawa.
sentences.article_title: US Marine indicted for murder and robbery of woman in Japan

sentences.text: Prosecutors have now indicted him for allegedly strangling Yagi with a telephone cord and then stealing her backpack and wallet on 3 October, media reports, citing the indictment document.
sentences.article_title: US Marine indicted for murder and robbery of woman in Japan

sentences.text: It wasreported Ballard had denied the allegations, but Asahi Shimbun and Kyodo News cited investigators saying he has made some statements suggesting involvement.
sentences.article_title: US Marine indicted for murder and robbery of woman in Japan

sentences.text: Security footage allegedly shows a man believed to be the suspect entering the hotel with the woman and leaving alone with her belongings.
sentences.article_title: US Marine indicted for murder and robbery of woman in Japan

sentences.text: Yagi's death has caused outrage in Japan, with Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi describing the crime as "brutal and heinous".
sentences.article_title: US Marine indicted for murder and robbery of woman in Japan

sentences.text: Earlier this month, the Marine Corps said it was "actively cooperating with Japanese authorities, in response to allegations of serious criminal actions by a Marine" and extended condolences to the victim's family.
sentences.article_title: US Marine indicted for murder and robbery of woman in Japan

sentences.text: It is the latest case involving a US serviceman in Okinawa, which hosts the highest concentration of around 55,000 US soldiers stationed in Japan.
sentences.article_title: US Marine indicted for murder and robbery of woman in Japan

sentences.text: Previous criminal cases have sparked anger and protests, the largest of which took place in 1995, when tens of thousands took to the streets following the abduction, beating and rape of a 12-year-old girl.
sentences.article_title: US Marine indicted for murder and robbery of woman in Japan

sentences.text: In 2024 alone, there were four sexual assault cases involving US troops in Okinawa, including that of air force member Brennon Washington, who was given five years for the rape and kidnapping of an underage girl.
sentences.article_title: US Marine indicted for murder and robbery of woman in Japan

sentences.text: In 2025, US marine Lance Cpl Jamel Clayton was sentenced to seven years in prison for sexually assaulting a woman.
sentences.article_title: US Marine indicted for murder and robbery of woman in Japan

sentences.text: Okinawa Governor Genta Koja said the prefecture has repeatedly demanded that the US take action to prevent such incidents, and said he sees the alleged crime as a sign of a lack of discipline.
sentences.article_title: US Marine indicted for murder and robbery of woman in Japan

sentences.text: The prime minister said her government has registered a "strong" protest with the US and called for "strict disciplinary action against US military personnel and thorough measures to prevent a recurrence of such incidents".
sentences.article_title: US Marine indicted for murder and robbery of woman in Japan

sentences.text: People in Japan have been voicing anger, with some 100 people protesting in both Naha and Tokyo earlier this month.
sentences.article_title: US Marine indicted for murder and robbery of woman in Japan

sentences.text: Others took to social media expressing their outrage and demanding justice, with one user saying: "Enough is enough." 'Not again': Arrest of US marine for murder reignites protests in Japan's Okinawa

sentences.text: Polling published on Friday suggests Gadi Eisenkot (left) is in a tight race with incumbent Benjamin Netanyahu (right) Israel heads to the polls on Tuesday for what many view as one of the most pivotal elections in the country's history.
sentences.article_title: How do Israel's elections work and who are the main contenders?

sentences.text: It's the first election since the 7 October 2023 Hamas-led attacks on Israel and its subsequent wars and conflicts across the region - in Gaza, Iran, Lebanon, Syria and Yemen.
sentences.article_title: How do Israel's elections work and who are the main contenders?

sentences.text: Polling published on Friday puts incumbent Benjamin Netanyahu in a tight race with Gadi Eisenkot, a former head of the Israel Defense Forces, to become prime minister.
sentences.article_title: How do Israel's elections work and who are the main contenders?

sentences.text: Eisenkot's popularity stems partly from his military credentials and his status as a relative political newcomer, having formed his Yashar Party only last year.
sentences.article_title: How do Israel's elections work and who are the main contenders?

sentences.text: He lost his son, a soldier, in the first months of the Gaza war, and served in Israel's war cabinet under Netanyahu until resigning in 2024 over his handling of the conflict.
sentences.article_title: How do Israel's elections work and who are the main contenders?

sentences.text: He has built his campaign on calls for accountability over the security failures that led to 7 October.
sentences.article_title: How do Israel's elections work and who are the main contenders?

sentences.text: Other opposition leaders include former prime minister Naftali Bennett and Avigdor Lieberman - both right-wingers who take hardline positions on security - and Yair Golan, a left-leaning former general.
sentences.article_title: How do Israel's elections work and who are the main contenders?

sentences.text: Despite their differences, they could work with Eisenkot to oust Netanyahu.
sentences.article_title: How do Israel's elections work and who are the main contenders?

sentences.text: Netanyahu's current government is the most right-wing in Israel's history.
sentences.article_title: How do Israel's elections work and who are the main contenders?

sentences.text: In order to remain in power, he will likely have to rely on the support of some of his existing far-right coalition partners.
sentences.article_title: How do Israel's elections work and who are the main contenders?

sentences.text: Some hold ultra-nationalist positions, such as calling for Israel to annex the West Bank and for the "migration" of Palestinians from Gaza, which could amount to the forced displacement of civilians.
sentences.article_title: How do Israel's elections work and who are the main contenders?

sentences.text: Some members of Netanyahu's own Likud party have also called for Palestinian "migration" from the territory.
sentences.article_title: How do Israel's elections work and who are the main contenders?

sentences.text: There are two Arab party blocs in the running too, as about one-fifth of Israel's population is Arab - many of whom describe themselves as Palestinian citizens of Israel.
sentences.article_title: How do Israel's elections work and who are the main contenders?

sentences.text: In theory, they could prove kingmakers.
sentences.article_title: How do Israel's elections work and who are the main contenders?

sentences.text: But all but one of the leading Jewish parties have ruled out working with them.
sentences.article_title: How do Israel's elections work and who are the main contenders?

sentences.text: How Arab parties could hold critical balance of power in Israeli election Israel's parliament - known as the Knesset - has 120 seats, meaning a government must hold 61 seats to command a majority.
sentences.article_title: How do Israel's elections work and who are the main contenders?

sentences.text: Israel uses a proportional representation voting system, so governments have always been coalitions of multiple parties.
sentences.article_title: How do Israel's elections work and who are the main contenders?

sentences.text: Friday's polling suggests neither Eisenkot or Netanyahu's blocs will reach a majority, meaning there may be weeks or months of political wrangling to come.
sentences.article_title: How do Israel's elections work and who are the main contenders?

sentences.text: If no bloc can form a majority, it is possible that a minority government could take power.
sentences.article_title: How do Israel's elections work and who are the main contenders?

sentences.text: And failing that, new elections could be called, with Netanyahu to remain as interim PM until then.
sentences.article_title: How do Israel's elections work and who are the main contenders?

sentences.text: The dominating topic has been security, with the challengers to Netanyahu all heavily criticising the security failures that led to the 7 October attacks, in which nearly 1,200 people were killed and 251 others taken back to Gaza as hostages.
sentences.article_title: How do Israel's elections work and who are the main contenders?

sentences.text: Nevertheless, Netanyahu has once again framed himself as "Mr Security", pointing to strategic victories in Israel's wars since 2023.
sentences.article_title: How do Israel's elections work and who are the main contenders?

sentences.text: Conscription is also a major topic.
sentences.article_title: How do Israel's elections work and who are the main contenders?

sentences.text: Historically, ultra-Orthodox Jewish men in full-time religious study have been exempt from military service, but since war broke out this has become an increasingly divisive policy.
sentences.article_title: How do Israel's elections work and who are the main contenders?

sentences.text: Judicial reform has also featured heavily during the campaign.
sentences.article_title: How do Israel's elections work and who are the main contenders?

sentences.text: Netanyahu's government is still pursuing contentious plans for reforms to the judicial system, which led to mass protests before 7 October.
sentences.article_title: How do Israel's elections work and who are the main contenders?

sentences.text: Critics say the plans would compromise the independence of the judiciary and threaten democracy.
sentences.article_title: How do Israel's elections work and who are the main contenders?

sentences.text: As in many countries, cost of living is another key issue.
sentences.article_title: How do Israel's elections work and who are the main contenders?

sentences.text: Food and housing costs have grown steadily in recent years.
sentences.article_title: How do Israel's elections work and who are the main contenders?

sentences.text: The bitter row over military service that could shape Israel's future A year on from the ceasefire in Gaza, Israel continues to carry out near-daily strikes on the territory - saying it is targeting Hamas operatives - and maintains control of more than half of it.
sentences.article_title: How do Israel's elections work and who are the main contenders?

sentences.text: More than 74,000 people have been killed in Israeli attacks on Gaza since 7 October 2023, according to the Hamas-run health ministry, whose figures are considered reliable by the UN.
sentences.article_title: How do Israel's elections work and who are the main contenders?

sentences.text: In the occupied West Bank, attacks by Jewish settlers are at an all-time high, according to UN records, while Israeli settlements, which are illegal under international law, are rapidly expanding.
sentences.article_title: How do Israel's elections work and who are the main contenders?

sentences.text: So for Palestinians, the shape of Israel's government is a major factor in their lives.
sentences.article_title: How do Israel's elections work and who are the main contenders?

sentences.text: On Gaza, Eisenkot does not differ hugely from Netanyahu.
sentences.article_title: How do Israel's elections work and who are the main contenders?

sentences.text: He recently pledged to end Hamas rule in the territory within 18 months, through a US-led peace plan or, if necessary, military means.
sentences.article_title: How do Israel's elections work and who are the main contenders?

sentences.text: In the West Bank, Netanyahu's camp largely wants to continue with its policy of rapid settlement expansion.
sentences.article_title: How do Israel's elections work and who are the main contenders?

sentences.text: Eisenkot supports Israeli settlements in general, but opposes proceeding with the controversial E1 settlement project which would, in effect, split the West Bank in two.
sentences.article_title: How do Israel's elections work and who are the main contenders?

sentences.text: He also wants to crack down on extremist Jewish settlers, and has spoken about creating the conditions for "autonomy or a state-minus" for Palestinians - under ultimate Israeli security control.
sentences.article_title: How do Israel's elections work and who are the main contenders?

sentences.text: For decades, many mainstream Israeli politicians advocated for a two-state solution - the creation of an independent Palestinian state in peaceful coexistence alongside Israel.
sentences.article_title: How do Israel's elections work and who are the main contenders?

sentences.text: But support for the idea has been declining for years.
sentences.article_title: How do Israel's elections work and who are the main contenders?

sentences.text: In this election, none of the leading Jewish parties are campaigning on it, and many have outright rejected it.
sentences.article_title: How do Israel's elections work and who are the main contenders?

sentences.text: Netanyahu has long vowed to block the idea.
sentences.article_title: How do Israel's elections work and who are the main contenders?

sentences.text: The Amos Channel sits between Rothschild Island (bottom centre) and Alexander Island, which is the larger landmass to the right Part of Antarctica has been named after former BBC science correspondent Jonathan Amos.

sentences.text: Leanne and Nathan Gregory on their wedding day The husband of a woman who died as she tried to rescue her two sons when they were swept out to sea in the Bahamas said they had been celebrating their 10th wedding anniversary.
sentences.article_title: Couple were celebrating anniversary before Bahamas tragedy

sentences.text: Leanne Gregory, from Stapleford in Nottinghamshire, had been on a family holiday with husband Nathan when he believes their boys were swept into the ocean by a riptide.
sentences.article_title: Couple were celebrating anniversary before Bahamas tragedy

sentences.text: Although the children were rescued from the water on Tuesday, their mother was unable to be saved, the Royal Bahamas Police Force said.
sentences.article_title: Couple were celebrating anniversary before Bahamas tragedy

sentences.text: Speaking to the BBC on Sunday, Nathan, who is now back home with their sons, said the trip had been an early celebration for their anniversary in December.
sentences.article_title: Couple were celebrating anniversary before Bahamas tragedy

sentences.text: Nathan said their relationship was perfect He said both boys had been so excited and been snorkelling in shallow water as they sorted out their towels and bags on the beach when the boys got into difficulties.
sentences.article_title: Couple were celebrating anniversary before Bahamas tragedy

sentences.text: Both parents went into the sea and tried to save them as they were swept out by the current, he added, and the whole ordeal happened in less than 10 minutes.
sentences.article_title: Couple were celebrating anniversary before Bahamas tragedy

sentences.text: Nathan said the loss of his 36-year-old "childhood sweetheart" was "unimaginable", but she was a "hero... in life and in death" as she helped to rescue the two boys.
sentences.article_title: Couple were celebrating anniversary before Bahamas tragedy

sentences.text: "I've known her since infant school," he told the BBC.
sentences.article_title: Couple were celebrating anniversary before Bahamas tragedy

sentences.text: "We first got together when we were 14... so 22 years." "There are no words I can use to describe Leanne, same as anyone she has ever known.
sentences.article_title: Couple were celebrating anniversary before Bahamas tragedy

sentences.text: "She was the purest of people, the most generous kind and beautiful person who ever walked the Earth.
sentences.article_title: Couple were celebrating anniversary before Bahamas tragedy

sentences.text: "Our relationship was perfect.
