sentences.text: Sharon Osbourne spoke to BBC News as the family prepares to release a film about Ozzy's final concert with Black Sabbath It's been 15 months since Ozzy Osbourne died, at the age of 76, at his home in Buckinghamshire.
sentences.article_title: Sharon Osbourne: 'I visit Ozzy's grave every day'

sentences.text: Although he had suffered from health problems for years, including Parkinson's disease and a fractured vertebra, his death was a shock.
sentences.article_title: Sharon Osbourne: 'I visit Ozzy's grave every day'

sentences.text: Less than three weeks beforehand, he had been on stage in Birmingham, playing a triumphant farewell concert.
sentences.article_title: Sharon Osbourne: 'I visit Ozzy's grave every day'

sentences.text: After the show, he was on a high.
sentences.article_title: Sharon Osbourne: 'I visit Ozzy's grave every day'

sentences.text: "He was just so, so happy," recalls his wife Sharon.
sentences.article_title: Sharon Osbourne: 'I visit Ozzy's grave every day'

sentences.text: "He was online, going through the reviews and saying, 'There's something terribly wrong', and I'm like, 'Why?' "He goes, 'I didn't get slagged by anybody.
sentences.article_title: Sharon Osbourne: 'I visit Ozzy's grave every day'

sentences.text: Why are people being nice to me?' "And I'm like, 'Because they like you'." On the morning he died, Ozzy had woken up early and gone downstairs for his usual morning workout.
sentences.article_title: Sharon Osbourne: 'I visit Ozzy's grave every day'

sentences.text: Shortly afterwards, he had a heart attack.
sentences.article_title: Sharon Osbourne: 'I visit Ozzy's grave every day'

sentences.text: An air ambulance was called and paramedics tried to save him.
sentences.article_title: Sharon Osbourne: 'I visit Ozzy's grave every day'

sentences.text: "I was asleep," says Sharon.
sentences.article_title: Sharon Osbourne: 'I visit Ozzy's grave every day'

sentences.text: "We'd spoken in the night.
sentences.article_title: Sharon Osbourne: 'I visit Ozzy's grave every day'

sentences.text: Ozzy had woken in the night and he asked me to kiss him twice, and I did.
sentences.article_title: Sharon Osbourne: 'I visit Ozzy's grave every day'

sentences.text: "And then he said, 'Hold me, hold me tight,' and I did.
sentences.article_title: Sharon Osbourne: 'I visit Ozzy's grave every day'

sentences.text: "And then the next thing I know, it's early in the morning, and someone comes rushing into the room saying, 'Come down now'.
sentences.article_title: Sharon Osbourne: 'I visit Ozzy's grave every day'

sentences.text: "I ran down, and that was it." Sharon and Ozzy Osbourne, pictured in 2017 after renewing their wedding vows The grief, she says, will never leave.
sentences.article_title: Sharon Osbourne: 'I visit Ozzy's grave every day'

sentences.text: "You've lost the love of your life, so you don't just wake up and go, 'I'm fine now.
sentences.article_title: Sharon Osbourne: 'I visit Ozzy's grave every day'

sentences.text: But you learn to live with it, and that's what I'm trying to do.
sentences.article_title: Sharon Osbourne: 'I visit Ozzy's grave every day'

sentences.text: So you either sit in a room and don't come out, or you accept it, befriend it, and that's it." The affection among Ozzy's fans was apparent before the singer's funeral.
sentences.article_title: Sharon Osbourne: 'I visit Ozzy's grave every day'

sentences.text: Thousands of people lined the streets of Birmingham, laying floral tributes and singing Black Sabbath songs as Ozzy's body was transported through his home city in a hearse topped by a purple floral tribute in the shape of a cross.
sentences.article_title: Sharon Osbourne: 'I visit Ozzy's grave every day'

sentences.text: Sharon says he would have been mystified by the outpouring of love.
sentences.article_title: Sharon Osbourne: 'I visit Ozzy's grave every day'

sentences.text: "He'd have been like, 'What's the matter with you guys?
sentences.article_title: Sharon Osbourne: 'I visit Ozzy's grave every day'

sentences.text: But for the family, the public response was a huge source of comfort.
sentences.article_title: Sharon Osbourne: 'I visit Ozzy's grave every day'

sentences.text: "There was no way I could put Ozzy in a public graveyard," she says.
sentences.article_title: Sharon Osbourne: 'I visit Ozzy's grave every day'

sentences.text: "I've seen what happens to other people in the public eye.
sentences.article_title: Sharon Osbourne: 'I visit Ozzy's grave every day'

sentences.text: There's no peace because people want to come and they want to pay their respects.
sentences.article_title: Sharon Osbourne: 'I visit Ozzy's grave every day'

sentences.text: That's an ongoing thing, and I wanted Ozzy to rest and just be." Does she visit him often?
sentences.article_title: Sharon Osbourne: 'I visit Ozzy's grave every day'

sentences.text: I can see him from my window." She still talks to him regularly, she says.
sentences.article_title: Sharon Osbourne: 'I visit Ozzy's grave every day'

sentences.text: Asked what she discusses, she puts a finger to her lips and gives a gentle "shh".
sentences.article_title: Sharon Osbourne: 'I visit Ozzy's grave every day'

sentences.text: Ozzy's family - including children Jack and Kelly - stopped to read the tributes during his funeral procession last July Ozzy and Sharon's relationship spanned more than 50 years.
sentences.article_title: Sharon Osbourne: 'I visit Ozzy's grave every day'

sentences.text: They met in 1970 and married in 1982.
sentences.article_title: Sharon Osbourne: 'I visit Ozzy's grave every day'

sentences.text: Their time together could be turbulent - he was arrested for attempting to murder her in 1989 (she dropped the charges), and they split briefly in 2016 amid rumours of infidelity - but the couple maintained that they were soulmates.
sentences.article_title: Sharon Osbourne: 'I visit Ozzy's grave every day'

sentences.text: "It was an unusual relationship because we had such highs and such terrible lows," she admits.
sentences.article_title: Sharon Osbourne: 'I visit Ozzy's grave every day'

sentences.text: But at the end of his life, "he knew" how much he was loved.
sentences.article_title: Sharon Osbourne: 'I visit Ozzy's grave every day'

sentences.text: You can see proof of that love - from his family, his fans and his bandmates – in a new documentary about his final gig at Birmingham's Villa Park last year, when he reunited with heavy rock legends Black Sabbath.
sentences.article_title: Sharon Osbourne: 'I visit Ozzy's grave every day'

sentences.text: Titled Back To The Beginning, it features more than 25 of the songs played at that star-studded concert, including Ozzy's solo set and Sabbath's entire performance.
sentences.article_title: Sharon Osbourne: 'I visit Ozzy's grave every day'

sentences.text: In backstage footage, fellow A-list performers discuss the star's influence in awestruck tones.
sentences.article_title: Sharon Osbourne: 'I visit Ozzy's grave every day'

sentences.text: "If there was no Sabbath, there's no Metallica," says the band's frontman James Hetfield.
sentences.article_title: Sharon Osbourne: 'I visit Ozzy's grave every day'

sentences.text: "It's as simple as that." Yungblud, whose version of Changes was one of the concert's emotional high points, talks about how, as a kid who didn't fit in, Ozzy changed his life.
sentences.article_title: Sharon Osbourne: 'I visit Ozzy's grave every day'

sentences.text: "The fact he was celebrated for his madness and his individuality gave me hope." sentences.text: Marcus Perkins said rising costs were making it harder for salons to employ staff and train apprentices After 22 years running a salon, Marcus Perkins says he is increasingly worried about the future of the hair and beauty industry.
sentences.article_title: Salon owners urge Budget VAT cut as staffing pressures grow

sentences.text: Rising costs are making it harder for businesses to employ staff and invest in apprenticeships, he says, while more salons are turning to self-employed models to survive.
sentences.article_title: Salon owners urge Budget VAT cut as staffing pressures grow

sentences.text: "Seeing salons close on the high street is very scary," he said.
sentences.article_title: Salon owners urge Budget VAT cut as staffing pressures grow

sentences.text: Luckily it hasn't happened yet but who knows what the future holds?" Perkins is among more than 2,000 salon owners who have signed an open letter calling on the Chancellor John Healey to cut VAT on hair and beauty services from 20% to 10% in this week's Budget.
sentences.article_title: Salon owners urge Budget VAT cut as staffing pressures grow

sentences.text: The letter is backed by the British Hair Consortium (BHC), which argues rising business costs are placing increasing pressure on traditional salon employers.
sentences.article_title: Salon owners urge Budget VAT cut as staffing pressures grow

sentences.text: However, the industry has also seen growing numbers of stylists move into self-employed arrangements, with hairdressers often renting a chair within a salon rather than being directly employed.
sentences.article_title: Salon owners urge Budget VAT cut as staffing pressures grow

sentences.text: With salon ownership perceived to be out of reach for many, self-employment offered independence, flexibility and higher earnings, industry research suggested , external .
sentences.article_title: Salon owners urge Budget VAT cut as staffing pressures grow

sentences.text: A Treasury spokesperson said hair and beauty businesses played an important role in supporting jobs, apprenticeships and thriving high streets.
sentences.article_title: Salon owners urge Budget VAT cut as staffing pressures grow

sentences.article_title: Salon owners urge Budget VAT cut as staffing pressures grow

sentences.text: While traditional salons said they faced rising pressures, a recent report from the British Beauty Council found that hair and beauty salons and shops made up almost a third of all leisure sites across UK retail centres.

sentences.article_title: Salon owners urge Budget VAT cut as staffing pressures grow

sentences.text: Lucy says she noticed changes in her skin and hair (left photo) alongside symptoms including fatigue and hair loss when her ferritin levels were low.

sentences.text: Lighting and shadows also play a part "Do you have ferritin face?" a young woman asks on TikTok, pointing to dark circles, washed-out skin and brittle hair, alongside before-and-after style photographs.

sentences.text: The content creator puts these features down to her iron levels.

sentences.text: It is one of a growing number of videos and posts on TikTok and Instagram claiming that low ferritin - a protein which stores iron in the body - can leave visible clues on your face.
sentences.article_title: Is 'ferritin face' a real thing - and can you really spot low iron from looks?

sentences.text: Users list pale or grey-looking skin, dark under-eye circles, dry or cracked lips, hair shedding and weak nails, while others share portraits claiming stark visual differences.
sentences.article_title: Is 'ferritin face' a real thing - and can you really spot low iron from looks?

sentences.text: The phrase "ferritin face" has spread widely across social media, with videos attracting millions of views.
sentences.article_title: Is 'ferritin face' a real thing - and can you really spot low iron from looks?

sentences.text: But doctors say appearance alone cannot diagnose iron deficiency.
sentences.article_title: Is 'ferritin face' a real thing - and can you really spot low iron from looks?

sentences.text: "Ferritin face is not a medical diagnosis," said GP Dr Aziza Sesay, who is based in the West Midlands.
sentences.article_title: Is 'ferritin face' a real thing - and can you really spot low iron from looks?

sentences.text: "However, it may be a clue to tell us that something is going on." Pale skin, hair shedding or brittle nails can accompany low iron, but can also be signs of other conditions, she told BBC News.
sentences.article_title: Is 'ferritin face' a real thing - and can you really spot low iron from looks?

sentences.text: Your ferritin levels show how good your body's iron stores are, while haemoglobin is the protein in red blood cells which carries oxygen.
sentences.article_title: Is 'ferritin face' a real thing - and can you really spot low iron from looks?

sentences.text: When haemoglobin is low, the blood cannot carry as much oxygen - a condition known as anaemia.
sentences.article_title: Is 'ferritin face' a real thing - and can you really spot low iron from looks?

sentences.text: But iron stores can become depleted before that happens, meaning someone can be iron-deficient and have symptoms without being anaemic.
sentences.article_title: Is 'ferritin face' a real thing - and can you really spot low iron from looks?

sentences.article_title: Is 'ferritin face' a real thing - and can you really spot low iron from looks?

sentences.text: Dr Sue Pavord, also a consultant haematologist, said iron deficiency is common and often under-diagnosed in women.
sentences.article_title: Is 'ferritin face' a real thing - and can you really spot low iron from looks?

sentences.text: Rosey Greenwood was asked to pay £1,906 because she took more than five minutes to pay for parking "I was completely on edge, every single day," said Rosey Greenwood.
sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.text: "I had letters coming through - I had debt collectors after me." Two years ago, Rosey was being told to pay £1,906 because she had taken too long to pay for parking.
sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.text: Rosey had paid every single time she parked at the Copeland Street car park in Derby, and had bank records to prove it.
sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.text: But Rosey had unknowingly broken the car park's terms and conditions, which stipulated that drivers must pay within five minutes of entering.
sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.text: Rosey could not afford to pay £1,906 - she was due to get married and also saving up to buy her first home.
sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.text: As she prepared to fight the case in court, her fiance emailed the BBC and asked us to "shed some light" on what was happening .
sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.text: The case was then raised in Parliament , external by Derby North MP Catherine Atkinson, who described the charges - which had caught out countless other motorists - as a "five-minute rip-off charge".
sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.text: The parking sector subsequently banned the five-minute payment rule by updating its code of practice , external , but the government is going further by bringing in a statutory Private Parking Code of Practice.
sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.text: "These charges leave people feeling ripped off and out of pocket, so I'm putting a stop to them," Prime Minister Andy Burnham said , external on Monday.
sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.text: But will the new code actually put the brakes on "rip-off" parking charges?
sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.text: Prime Minister Andy Burnham said parking charges left people "feeling ripped off" The government's new Private Parking Code of Practice was laid out in Parliament on Tuesday.
sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.text: It sets out standards that parking operators must follow.
sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.text: Housing and communities minister Florence Eshalomi said , external the new code "will give drivers a range of rights and protections to make these unfair practices a thing of the past".
sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.text: The code is now subject to a 40-day period of parliamentary scrutiny, during which MPs and peers can object before it is formally issued.
sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.text: The code will then come into force 21 calendar days from the point of issue.
sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.text: The five-minute payment rule - as stipulated on this sign - had already been banned by the parking sector itself In places, the code appears to be very similar to the private parking sector's existing code of practice , external .
sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.text: For example, Eshalomi said drivers would "now have a guaranteed minimum five minutes to decide whether to park", known as the consideration period.
sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.text: However, the sector's code already gives drivers a minimum consideration period of five minutes, so this does not appear to be new.
sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.text: The government's code also gives drivers a 10-minute grace period , external in which to leave a car park following the end of their permitted stay.
sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.text: However, the sector's code already gives drivers a 10-minute grace period, so this does not appear to be new either.
sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.text: The government's code sets the maximum parking charge at £100, or £60 if paid within a fortnight.
sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.text: This is also the same as in the sector's code.
sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.text: The government's code states charges should be reduced to £20 on appeal , external under four circumstances: not displaying a parking permit despite having a valid one, entering the wrong vehicle registration into a parking machine, not entering a registration at all, and not displaying a Blue Badge despite having one.
sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.text: The sector's code already said charges should be reduced to £20 under those circumstances.
sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.text: Parking operators will also still be allowed to add a £70 debt recovery fee , external to each parking charge if drivers do not pay, as well as court fees and legal costs.
sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.text: In contrast, the sector's code said these charges should be reduced to £20.
sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.text: The government's code says parking operators who do not comply will lose access to DVLA vehicle keeper data, meaning they will no longer be able to issue parking charges.
sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.text: This is meant to happen already, because parking operators need to be members of one of two trade associations in order to access DVLA data, and they can theoretically lose their membership if they break the rules.
sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.text: Campaigners claim this has not happened in practice, but the government insists it will happen in future.
sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.text: There will also be what the government describes as a "fully independent Scrutiny and Oversight Board".
sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.text: Jack Cousens, head of roads policy at the AA, said the benefit of the new code was that it was backed by the government, rather than the parking sector itself.
sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.text: "That means, if there are any changes to be made, it will come via the government and indeed via the independent scrutiny panel," he added.
sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.text: "Up until now, the private industry have held the pen on changing the code of practice.
sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.text: Now the pen is firmly in the hand of the government." Lynda Eagan does not believe the new code will lead to fewer parking charge notices being issued Both the AA and RAC have welcomed the statutory code of practice - which they campaigned for - but believe it does not go far enough.
sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.text: For example, the AA believes there needs to be a single and independent appeals process.
sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.text: "Drivers need to have confidence that when they are making their representations, it's being heard by an independent body, as opposed to the private parking operators and their trade bodies marking their own homework," Cousens said.
sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.text: The AA also believes the government needs to find an alternative to debt recovery fees and charges, which often "spiral" into the threat of court action and County Court Judgments.
sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.text: This was how Rosey was asked to pay a total of £1,906 for 10 parking charges, and also how Hannah Robinson was asked to pay £11,390 .
sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.text: The RAC shares the same concerns.
sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.text: "We've long called for the banning of debt recovery fees being added on top of parking charge notices, and a single independent appeals body to replace the two industry-run ones, but neither have been included [in the code] which is disappointing," head of policy Simon Williams said.
sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.text: Parking campaigner Lynda Eagan, who helped Rosey, is sceptical about how much has changed.
sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.text: "I've been screaming at the TV every time I see someone saying 'we've got these new things'," she said.
sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.text: "They've tweaked a few things here and there, but it's not actually going to make an awful lot of difference to people.
sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.text: "How, when not much has really changed, is that going to reduce the number of PCNs [parking charge notices]?" In response, a Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government spokesperson said: "We don't accept these claims.
sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.text: We've introduced a new Private Parking Code of Practice that will have statutory force and independent oversight.
sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.text: The AA is more optimistic.
sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.text: "We are hopeful that it could make some difference to some drivers, and we hope that it stops some of the more spurious claims being stopped at source, but we will be watching," Cousens said.

She said retaining a £100 parking charge was important.
sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.text: A spokesperson for the International Parking Community (IPC) said: "The IPC has long supported a code that raises standards, and we are now reviewing it in detail to understand what it means for motorists, landowners and operators alike.
sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: Making sure workers give their consent and are comfortable with the process is important, he says.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: And until recently, that data was not available.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: "There is no existing internet archive of embodied human activity - no dataset of a kitchen being cleaned, or a car being assembled by hands that know exactly how much force to apply.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: That data has to be captured from scratch, in the real world, across diverse environments," says Agarwal, whose company has bases in Bangalore and San Francisco.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: At the moment his firm has 96,000 data collectors across countries in Latin America and Southeast Asia.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: "You need to source across a variety of factories, a variety of tasks, in different geographies because if you want to build deployment for US factories or US houses, you'd want environments that are a proxy for that.

sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: "Garments stitching and cutting.

sentences.text: Crime scene evidence is often not enough to identify suspects Randy Gail Sperino was last seen alive on the evening of 9 November 1993, as she was getting into a pickup truck in Granite City, Illinois.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: The 34-year-old's body was found hours later in a field nearby, the victim of blunt force trauma.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: The identity of her killer was a mystery.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: DNA evidence found at the crime scene was tested against standard law enforcement databases, but no matches were found.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: For three decades, investigators from the Madison County Sheriff's Office chased leads and interviewed hundreds of people as they attempted to identify the perpetrator.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: The case looked like it would remain one of more than 250,000 unsolved homicides in the US.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: Then, last year, detectives tried a fresh approach.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: They sent genetic evidence to Othram, a Houston-based company that uses DNA technology to help identify the perpetrators in cold and current crime cases.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: The Madison County detectives had been inspired by investigative genetic genealogy techniques used to identify the Golden State Killer, Joseph James DeAngelo, back in 2018.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: In that case, an investigative team constructed a family tree to help identify the killer.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: They were able to do so thanks to DNA data that relatives had provided to commercial databases, similar to consumer ancestry platforms.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: Unlike traditional forensic DNA testing, which generally relies on a direct comparison between evidence and a known person, investigative genetic genealogy can identify distant genetic relatives of an unknown individual.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: Othram set about applying this technique to track down Sperino's killer.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: While the suspect's own DNA profile wasn't available, profiles submitted by his extended relatives allowed the company to identify a male family member.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: "That lead broke the case open," said Captain Tim Lawrence of Madison County Sheriff's Office, which was responsible for investigating the crime.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: It was a crucial clue that led the detectives to Albert "Buddy" Zigler, 70, who police say then confessed to the murder.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: He was charged in May this year.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: Wes Sperino, Gail's son, said at a press conference: "I finally get closure and I finally know who did this." Albert Zigler was charged with murder in May The technique that led detectives to Zigler is credited with revolutionising how forensic cases are solved.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: It has been highly successful in helping solve cases involving unidentified human remains and identifying suspects in longstanding investigations.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: One of the challenges facing detectives on major investigations like the hunt for Sperino's attacker is the sheer amount of evidence they dig up.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: Officers investigating her murder realised AI could help them wade through the mountains of evidence they had accumulated since 1993.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: They used a platform called Centerline AI, from Florida software company CentralSquare, to analyse more than 2,000 pages of records and identify evidence for the DNA testing that helped to break the case.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: The AI helped them reconstruct timelines and organise witness information.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: "It's so much easier than having a detective have to read through 2,000 pages," Lawrence says.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: His team could interact with the AI like a chat bot.

sentences.text: This also helped when it came to interviewing Zigler after they had tracked him down.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: Detectives were able to ask questions of the AI to help "figure out if Zigler was being truthful", says Lawrence.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: But the technology is "only as good as the investigator," says the captain.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: There comes a point, he says, "where you leave the technology behind and you have to go track people down and talk to them." Investigative genetic genealogy has its limitations too.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: Mittelman says: "It can't solve every case.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: If you have no DNA, you can't really use this technique." "But this technique is a lot more powerful and a lot more likely to yield identities than having to rely on the chance that you find a match somewhere in a database," he adds.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: Eddie Lever was able to leave his tenancy more easily because of the Renters' Rights Act When the Renters' Rights Act came into force in May it was described as the biggest change for tenants in England in a generation, giving more stability and security to the millions of people who rent from private landlords.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: The legislation has also prompted a shake-up of the student rental market, which has posed challenges for landlords as it allows people to leave a tenancy rather than being tied in for the full academic year.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: Eddie Lever had finished his first year at the University of Exeter when he decided the course wasn't for him.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: The 20-year-old wanted to switch to studying international relations at the University of York but had already organised his house for the upcoming year.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: The tenancy was signed and had started.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: But because of changes in the Renters' Rights Act, Eddie only had to give two months' notice before he could leave and stop paying rent.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: The legislation ended fixed-term tenancies - where renters are tied in to contracts for a specific number of months.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: For students, previously contracts were generally for the full academic year.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: Instead, properties are now rented on a rolling basis, which means tenants pay rent weekly or monthly with no fixed end date.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: University-owned halls of residence and Purpose-Built Student Accommodation are exempt , external and can still offer fixed-term contracts so this change primarily affects students renting from a private landlord.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: "If the Renters' Rights Act wasn't a thing, I don't think I would have been able to move universities because I would have been locked into the full [year] contract," Eddie explains.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: Fortunately, Eddie had a friend who was looking for a room who was able to take his place so his housemates could sign a new tenancy.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: He acknowledges the situation would have been more difficult for his housemates if there wasn't someone who could take his room.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: However, Eddie thinks the benefits for students are worth this risk.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: "If you were to fall out with your flatmates or if you decide that university is not for you, being locked into a full-term contract can be really prohibitive financially," he says.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: "So without that flexibility, people can really be locked into situations that they don't necessarily want to be in." Lewis Wilson, vice president for higher education at the National Union of Students, says this flexibility means students can also save money on rent by moving home for the summer.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: While previously, many student rental contracts ran into the summer after courses had finished, students can now choose to move out earlier if they want.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: Wilson says students also benefit from wider changes in the act, which bans landlords in England from evicting tenants without a reason.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: Campaigners argue this gives renters greater security and confidence to ask for repairs, without fearing they could be evicted if they raise concerns.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: Lewis Wilson from the NUS says the legislation has given students more freedom to move out when they want However, greater flexibility for students to leave tenancies also means less certainty for landlords.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: The act did introduce a specific ground , external for landlords to evict a group of students at the end of the academic year if they intend to re-let the property to students.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: Chris Norris, chief policy officer at the National Residential Landlords Association, says the bigger problem for student landlords is if their tenants choose to move out earlier.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: He argues this is a bigger risk for students - who may fall out with their housemates or drop out of university - than, for example, families, who are less likely to want to move out after just a few months.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: Norris says the end of fixed-term tenancies means student houses could be left empty over the summer after courses finish - or even earlier.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: He adds that it is now more difficult for student landlords to rent a house for just a few months as they don't know how long the tenants will stay and can't guarantee it will be available for students again in the autumn.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: Norris says it's early days for the new legislation and many landlords are taking this year as a test to see how these issues play out in practice.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: However, he warns that some may choose to increase the monthly rent they charge to cover the risk of their properties being empty over the summer.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: In some cases, he says landlords may even sell up or stop renting to students, reducing supply and pushing up prices.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: While Sue says she doesn't want to put up her prices, if her houses end up being empty over the summer because students decide to end their tenancy after their final exams she says she may have to.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: She has already brought forward the start of her tenancy agreements to August instead of September to try and reduce the risks of this.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: However, she says if her tenants move out earlier in the year she would struggle to make a profit, whilst covering costs including her mortgage, council tax and utility standing charges when the properties are empty.

sentences.text: Anthony Lee and his wife Laura pleaded guilty at Southwark Crown Court on Thursday The Conservatives' former director of campaigning and his wife have received suspended prison sentences after they admitted to cheating at gambling by placing bets on the date of the 2024 general election.
sentences.article_title: Ex-Tory campaign chief and his wife receive suspended sentences over election bets

sentences.text: Anthony Lee used "inside information" emerging from a private meeting called by then-Prime Minister Rishi Sunak to bet on the general election date months before it took place, Southwark Crown Court heard.
sentences.article_title: Ex-Tory campaign chief and his wife receive suspended sentences over election bets

sentences.text: Lee and his wife Laura stood to win more than £23,000 had their cheating not been uncovered, the court heard.
sentences.article_title: Ex-Tory campaign chief and his wife receive suspended sentences over election bets

sentences.text: Lee was sentenced to 10 months and two weeks' imprisonment, suspended for 12 months, while his wife was sentenced to four months and two weeks' imprisonment, suspended for a year.
sentences.article_title: Ex-Tory campaign chief and his wife receive suspended sentences over election bets

sentences.text: Amy Hind, a former Tory party employee who was working as an NHS business support manager, was also sentenced to six months' imprisonment, suspended for a year, after previously pleading guilty to cheating on the date of the election.
sentences.article_title: Ex-Tory campaign chief and his wife receive suspended sentences over election bets

sentences.text: Judge Tony Baumgartner, sentencing the three of them, said their conduct "risked undermining" the confidence the public has in the Conservative Party "as an institution", "undermining trust in the democratic process" and the "integrity of the gambling system".
sentences.article_title: Ex-Tory campaign chief and his wife receive suspended sentences over election bets

sentences.text: The trio were among several people charged with betting offences by the Gambling Commission.
sentences.article_title: Ex-Tory campaign chief and his wife receive suspended sentences over election bets

sentences.text: The trials of other defendants will take place next year and in 2028.
sentences.article_title: Ex-Tory campaign chief and his wife receive suspended sentences over election bets

sentences.text: Former Conservative MP Craig Williams, who was Sunak's closest parliamentary aide at the time, pleaded guilty in June and will be sentenced at a later date.
sentences.article_title: Ex-Tory campaign chief and his wife receive suspended sentences over election bets

sentences.text: Sunak's decision to call a general election for July 2024 was a surprise to many, including several Conservative MPs, who were expecting an autumn date.
sentences.article_title: Ex-Tory campaign chief and his wife receive suspended sentences over election bets

sentences.text: The court heard that Sunak held a private Downing Street meeting on 10 March of that year to discuss possible dates.
sentences.article_title: Ex-Tory campaign chief and his wife receive suspended sentences over election bets

sentences.text: Neither Lee nor his wife attended the meeting, but the couple began betting online on the election being held in July or between July and September, the court heard.
sentences.article_title: Ex-Tory campaign chief and his wife receive suspended sentences over election bets

sentences.text: Baumgartner described Anthony Lee as a "central figure" in the preparation of the general election, who sat at a group of desks within Tory HQ known as the "God Pod".
sentences.article_title: Ex-Tory campaign chief and his wife receive suspended sentences over election bets

sentences.text: Representing Lee, barrister Richard Pratt said his client did not concretely know the working date of the election, saying it "still represented a gamble from his point of view".
sentences.article_title: Ex-Tory campaign chief and his wife receive suspended sentences over election bets

sentences.text: The barrister told the court: "It was always possible the prime minister could change his mind." Pratt said there "wasn't any direct manipulation" by the defendant.
sentences.article_title: Ex-Tory campaign chief and his wife receive suspended sentences over election bets

sentences.text: Laura Lee worked for the Tories as their "head of international" and had been selected as the party candidate for Bristol North West for the election.
sentences.article_title: Ex-Tory campaign chief and his wife receive suspended sentences over election bets

sentences.text: Baumgartner said she had no involvement in the election planning and her access to information "came predominantly" from her husband.
sentences.article_title: Ex-Tory campaign chief and his wife receive suspended sentences over election bets

sentences.text: The court heard Hind's husband Anthony worked as a deputy digital director for the Conservatives but did not place any bets himself.
sentences.article_title: Ex-Tory campaign chief and his wife receive suspended sentences over election bets

sentences.text: Baumgartner said Hind's husband "was party to emails relating to the forthcoming general election and was one potential source of your inside information".
sentences.article_title: Ex-Tory campaign chief and his wife receive suspended sentences over election bets

sentences.text: The judge later said "someone else who worked within the heart of CCHQ" could have given her the "highly confidential" information.
sentences.article_title: Ex-Tory campaign chief and his wife receive suspended sentences over election bets

sentences.text: The court heard Hind placed four bets and made three further unsuccessful attempts to place bets.
sentences.article_title: Ex-Tory campaign chief and his wife receive suspended sentences over election bets

sentences.text: The unsuccessful attempts were for £767, £700 and £750.
sentences.article_title: Ex-Tory campaign chief and his wife receive suspended sentences over election bets

sentences.text: Baumgartner described them all as having expressed remorse for their actions.
sentences.article_title: Ex-Tory campaign chief and his wife receive suspended sentences over election bets

sentences.text: The trio are now subject to a 12-month prohibited activity requirement, banning them from accessing or using online gambling websites or applications.
sentences.article_title: Ex-Tory campaign chief and his wife receive suspended sentences over election bets

sentences.text: Anthony Lee was ordered to complete 100 hours of unpaid work and pay more than £6,600 in compensation to a betting company, while Laura Lee must carry out 40 hours of unpaid work and pay £4,265.
sentences.article_title: Ex-Tory campaign chief and his wife receive suspended sentences over election bets

sentences.text: Hind was ordered to complete 50 hours of unpaid work.
sentences.article_title: Ex-Tory campaign chief and his wife receive suspended sentences over election bets

sentences.article_title: Ex-Tory campaign chief and his wife receive suspended sentences over election bets

sentences.text: Adrianne says her chronic UTI has impacted her physically and mentally "The impact goes far beyond what people understand - we're talking about pain, urgency, sleepless nights and missing out on your life," Adrianne tells her roughly 8,000 followers in a video on TikTok.

sentences.text: For nearly five years, Adrianne has lived with a chronic urinary tract infection (UTI) - a condition it took her two years to get a diagnosis for.
sentences.article_title: Chronic UTIs affect millions in the UK - these women are out to end the stigma

sentences.text: In that time she was wrongly told it was colon cancer, Crohn's disease or even that her partner must have been cheating and had given her a sexually transmitted infection.
sentences.article_title: Chronic UTIs affect millions in the UK - these women are out to end the stigma

sentences.text: What started as one UTI in 2022 became a debilitating cycle.
sentences.article_title: Chronic UTIs affect millions in the UK - these women are out to end the stigma

sentences.text: "It has completely stripped me of everything: being able to work properly, my relationships, my friendships, going out, being able to have a normal social life," says Adrianne, who works in digital marketing in London.
sentences.article_title: Chronic UTIs affect millions in the UK - these women are out to end the stigma

sentences.text: The 29-year-old was eventually diagnosed privately with a chronic UTI - something experts estimate could affect up to 1.7 million women in the UK , external .
sentences.article_title: Chronic UTIs affect millions in the UK - these women are out to end the stigma

sentences.text: Men and children are also affected.
sentences.article_title: Chronic UTIs affect millions in the UK - these women are out to end the stigma

sentences.text: Adrianne is not alone in sharing her story and coping mechanisms on social media to fight the stigma surrounding UTIs.
sentences.article_title: Chronic UTIs affect millions in the UK - these women are out to end the stigma

sentences.text: A quick search on Tiktok or Instagram shows hundreds of posts of women of all ages talking about the reality of living with recurrent and chronic UTIs.
sentences.article_title: Chronic UTIs affect millions in the UK - these women are out to end the stigma

sentences.text: "I felt incredibly nervous to put myself out there, but there's now this community of people who can share tips with each other, and understand each other," said Adrianne, saying her posts have had a "really positive response".

sentences.text: This video can not be played Like ‘weeing lava’: Living with chronic UTIs A chronic UTI, which has no official medical definition, is an infection with persistent symptoms - even after a standard course of antibiotics.

sentences.text: While sending a urine sample to the lab remains the gold standard to diagnose a UTI, "false negatives" can often occur, says Professor Chris Harding, a consultant urologist at Newcastle upon Tyne Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust.
sentences.article_title: Chronic UTIs affect millions in the UK - these women are out to end the stigma

sentences.text: Another hurdle is the significant crossover between chronic UTIs and other conditions such as painful bladder syndrome, chronic pelvic pain and endometriosis, says Magda Kujawa, a consultant urologist at Stockport NHS Foundation Trust.

sentences.text: Adrianne says she felt "dismissed" by doctors while trying to get a diagnosis, and frustrated at repeatedly being given advice around hygiene and hydration, while her symptoms persisted.
sentences.article_title: Chronic UTIs affect millions in the UK - these women are out to end the stigma

sentences.text: Both experts say health professionals should listen to the patient's story to understand whether symptoms amount to a recurrent or chronic condition or something else entirely.
sentences.article_title: Chronic UTIs affect millions in the UK - these women are out to end the stigma

sentences.text: Since she started posting online, Adrianne has received messages from other young women who worry they are "dirty" and "not taking care of themselves" or that there is "something wrong with them".
sentences.article_title: Chronic UTIs affect millions in the UK - these women are out to end the stigma

sentences.text: "There's definitely still a lot of stigma around why people get them (UTIs), and it all just comes back to education.

sentences.article_title: Chronic UTIs affect millions in the UK - these women are out to end the stigma

sentences.article_title: Chronic UTIs affect millions in the UK - these women are out to end the stigma

sentences.text: Pope Leo returned to St Peter's Square on Wednesday for his weekly general audience Pope Leo XIV does not need any further treatment following an operation to remove a cancerous growth from his lung, his doctors have said.
sentences.article_title: Pope does not need further treatment after lung cancer surgery

sentences.text: Test results on tissue removed during surgery confirmed he had had a lung adenocarcinoma, as was initially diagnosed, and that the disease was localised, according to a statement shared by the Vatican.
sentences.article_title: Pope does not need further treatment after lung cancer surgery

sentences.text: "A subsequent oncological assessment has confirmed that no further treatment is necessary," it added.
sentences.article_title: Pope does not need further treatment after lung cancer surgery

sentences.text: The 71-year-old was discharged from Rome's Gemelli Hospital over the weekend four days after his operation - stopping to speak to well-wishers as he left the grounds.
sentences.article_title: Pope does not need further treatment after lung cancer surgery

sentences.text: It comes as he held his first weekly general audience since leaving hospital at St Peter's Square on Wednesday.
sentences.article_title: Pope does not need further treatment after lung cancer surgery

sentences.text: The surgery, which took place on 13 October and lasted for 90 minutes, included the removal of the lower lobe of the Pope's right lung.
sentences.article_title: Pope does not need further treatment after lung cancer surgery

sentences.text: The pontiff himself had announced during his weekly Sunday prayers that he would be having the procedure - telling those gathered in St Peter's Square that doctors had found a nodule on his lung.
sentences.article_title: Pope does not need further treatment after lung cancer surgery

sentences.text: He said at the time that it had been caught "at an early stage".
sentences.article_title: Pope does not need further treatment after lung cancer surgery

sentences.text: Images shared days after his operation, on Friday, showed the Pope celebrating Mass from the hospital wearing green vestments and standing behind a makeshift altar.
sentences.article_title: Pope does not need further treatment after lung cancer surgery

sentences.text: On the same day, the Vatican said he spoke to Russian President Vladimir Putin over the phone to urge a ceasefire in the blockaded Russian-occupied Ukrainian city of Oleshky to allow the delivery of food aid, and to call for "dialogue and peace".
sentences.article_title: Pope does not need further treatment after lung cancer surgery

sentences.text: The pontiff had a similar phone call with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky on Monday.
sentences.article_title: Pope does not need further treatment after lung cancer surgery

sentences.text: Those close to the Pope have also previously said he was keen not to delay a trip to Latin America which is planned for early November.
sentences.article_title: Pope does not need further treatment after lung cancer surgery

sentences.text: A clinical trial has been launched in the UK which scientists hope could cut years from the search for new treatments for Alzheimer's disease.
sentences.article_title: Diabetes and ADHD drugs to be tested on Alzheimer's patients in new study

sentences.text: It will test multiple drugs simultaneously, starting with two repurposed medicines already used to treat type 2 diabetes and attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD).
sentences.article_title: Diabetes and ADHD drugs to be tested on Alzheimer's patients in new study

sentences.text: The study will examine whether the drugs can lessen symptoms such as memory and thinking problems, and help people maintain their quality of life.
sentences.article_title: Diabetes and ADHD drugs to be tested on Alzheimer's patients in new study

sentences.text: Angela Bucksey, 67, from Cambridgeshire, was diagnosed with Alzheimer's in January and is the first person to begin treatment on the trial, called AD-SMART.
sentences.article_title: Diabetes and ADHD drugs to be tested on Alzheimer's patients in new study

sentences.text: "We have Alzheimer's in the family," she told the BBC.
sentences.article_title: Diabetes and ADHD drugs to be tested on Alzheimer's patients in new study

sentences.text: "My mother had it and my aunts, so it was a disappointment rather than a shock when I was diagnosed because I knew it would restrict my life.
sentences.article_title: Diabetes and ADHD drugs to be tested on Alzheimer's patients in new study

sentences.text: "But I was determined that it wasn't going to define me." Angela said she felt empowered joining the trial because "at least you are doing something".
sentences.article_title: Diabetes and ADHD drugs to be tested on Alzheimer's patients in new study

sentences.text: "Instead of just sitting there, you're standing up and saying, I will fight back." Alzheimer's is the most common type of dementia, affecting around 600,000 people in the UK.
sentences.article_title: Diabetes and ADHD drugs to be tested on Alzheimer's patients in new study

sentences.text: Prime Minister Andy Burnham, whose father died from Alzheimer's last month, said he knew how it felt to lose a loved one to dementia, and had seen first-hand the devastating impact of the disease on families.
sentences.article_title: Diabetes and ADHD drugs to be tested on Alzheimer's patients in new study

sentences.text: "That's why I'm proud to see this trial being launched in the UK, so that cutting-edge treatments can reach patients here as soon as possible," he said.
sentences.article_title: Diabetes and ADHD drugs to be tested on Alzheimer's patients in new study

sentences.text: The AD-SMART study is what's known as a multi-arm, multi-stage platform trial where several treatments are tested simultaneously, with the results compared with one group of participants taking a placebo or dummy.
sentences.article_title: Diabetes and ADHD drugs to be tested on Alzheimer's patients in new study

sentences.text: This means those involved have a higher likelihood of getting an active treatment than in a traditional trial.
sentences.article_title: Diabetes and ADHD drugs to be tested on Alzheimer's patients in new study

sentences.text: If any drug isn't showing benefit it can be dropped quickly and a new treatment added in its place - the approach has been used successfully in cancer and motor neurone disease.
sentences.article_title: Diabetes and ADHD drugs to be tested on Alzheimer's patients in new study

sentences.text: The two initial drugs being tested are metformin, used to treat type 2 diabetes, and atomoxetine, for ADHD, which were selected by an international panel of experts.
sentences.article_title: Diabetes and ADHD drugs to be tested on Alzheimer's patients in new study

sentences.text: Both drugs may help reduce brain inflammation, which is a driver of neurodegeneration, said chief investigator Prof Paresh Malhotra, group leader at the UK Dementia Research Institute Centre for Care Research & Technology at Imperial College London.
sentences.article_title: Diabetes and ADHD drugs to be tested on Alzheimer's patients in new study

sentences.text: "For too long, Alzheimer's research has moved at the pace of one drug, one trial, one answer - sometimes taking a decade or more before we know if we've found something that works," he told the BBC.
sentences.article_title: Diabetes and ADHD drugs to be tested on Alzheimer's patients in new study

sentences.text: "We are applying advances from cancer and other conditions to accelerate testing of treatments for people with Alzheimer's disease." For the drugs to be successful, the study has to show that they have beneficial effects on thinking and the ability to carry out everyday activities.
sentences.article_title: Diabetes and ADHD drugs to be tested on Alzheimer's patients in new study

sentences.text: "That's what patients and their carers care about," said Prof Malhotra.
sentences.article_title: Diabetes and ADHD drugs to be tested on Alzheimer's patients in new study

sentences.text: Some 1,200 participants with mild to moderate Alzheimer's will be recruited at more than 30 sites across the UK.
sentences.article_title: Diabetes and ADHD drugs to be tested on Alzheimer's patients in new study

sentences.text: Sites in Cambridgeshire, Surrey, London, Southampton and Edinburgh are already open.
sentences.article_title: Diabetes and ADHD drugs to be tested on Alzheimer's patients in new study

sentences.text: Scientists expect to finish evaluating the first drugs in 2030 and, in that time, additional treatments are likely to be added.
sentences.article_title: Diabetes and ADHD drugs to be tested on Alzheimer's patients in new study

sentences.text: All the participants will have regular health checks including cognitive tests, which will help researchers assess how effective the treatments are.
sentences.article_title: Diabetes and ADHD drugs to be tested on Alzheimer's patients in new study

sentences.text: Angela Bucksey's husband Steve, who is her study partner, told the BBC: "Joining the trial has brought us back from the despair of a diagnosis which everybody recognises is non-recoverable.
sentences.article_title: Diabetes and ADHD drugs to be tested on Alzheimer's patients in new study

sentences.text: People with a confirmed Alzheimer's diagnosis who would like to take part can register their interest on the AD-SMART website , external .
sentences.article_title: Diabetes and ADHD drugs to be tested on Alzheimer's patients in new study

sentences.text: The trial is being led by the UK Dementia Research Institute and Alzheimer's Research UK.
sentences.article_title: Diabetes and ADHD drugs to be tested on Alzheimer's patients in new study

sentences.text: Partners include the National Institute for Health and Care Research, the Medical Research Council and Health Data Research UK, with funding by UK government.
sentences.article_title: Diabetes and ADHD drugs to be tested on Alzheimer's patients in new study

sentences.text: Perran Moon has referred himself to be investigated A second Labour MP, Perran Moon, has been suspended over Covid loan repayments, after voluntarily referring himself for investigation.
sentences.article_title: Second Labour MP suspended over Covid loan repayments

sentences.text: Moon, the MP for Camborne and Redruth, is listed on Companies House as the co-director of a training company called Autoswot , external , which last filed accounts in June 2021.
sentences.article_title: Second Labour MP suspended over Covid loan repayments

sentences.text: Government Bounce Back Loans of up to £50,000 were made available to support small businesses during the pandemic, but a government report found the scheme was vulnerable to fraud and error.
sentences.article_title: Second Labour MP suspended over Covid loan repayments

sentences.text: In August, Labour MP Bayo Alaba was suspended after queries about a Covid-era loan, and a third MP, James McMurdock, quit Reform in 2025 after questions about eligibility for loans he received.
sentences.article_title: Second Labour MP suspended over Covid loan repayments

sentences.text: Bounce back loans worth a total of £46bn were issued when the scheme was launched in May 2020, making it the biggest of the government's pandemic-era loan schemes.
sentences.article_title: Second Labour MP suspended over Covid loan repayments

sentences.text: Each one had a 100% government guarantee, meaning taxpayers' cash was used to pay back banks if the companies failed, but the Covid counter-fraud commissioner later found total fraud and error estimated at up to £2.8bn to the public purse.
sentences.article_title: Second Labour MP suspended over Covid loan repayments

sentences.text: Autoswot had been set up in June 2019, a year before the loans became available, and at that time had forecast revenues of more than £200,000.
sentences.article_title: Second Labour MP suspended over Covid loan repayments

sentences.text: Moon stressed he had applied for the maximum loan of £50,000 within the rules, regularly seeking professional advice about its obligations, and would provide documents to the Labour Party investigation into the matter.
sentences.article_title: Second Labour MP suspended over Covid loan repayments

sentences.text: He said the loan was used to pay for "staffing and other essential business costs" during the pandemic and partial repayments were made until the company ceased trading in late 2022.
sentences.article_title: Second Labour MP suspended over Covid loan repayments

sentences.text: The BBC understands that Moon was repeatedly assured in writing by Companies House that no accounts needed to be filed after the company applied to be struck off, but that guidance was incorrect.
sentences.article_title: Second Labour MP suspended over Covid loan repayments

sentences.text: Moon, who was first elected in the 2024 Labour landslide following a career in communications and marketing, said the business folded due to unforeseen external market pressures and "despite the best efforts of staff".
sentences.article_title: Second Labour MP suspended over Covid loan repayments

sentences.text: He said: "In order for these matters to be looked into, I have voluntarily referred myself to the Labour Party's investigations process and will cooperate fully with this process.
sentences.article_title: Second Labour MP suspended over Covid loan repayments

sentences.text: "The loan application was made in good faith, and the information provided, including the company's turnover forecast, was accurate and properly based.
sentences.article_title: Second Labour MP suspended over Covid loan repayments

sentences.text: "I will continue to work hard every day representing my constituents while this party process is ongoing." A Labour Party spokesperson confirmed Moon had referred himself for investigation.
sentences.article_title: Second Labour MP suspended over Covid loan repayments

sentences.text: "The Labour Party expects the highest standards from our elected representatives and we have robust processes in place to ensure those high standards are upheld," they said.
sentences.article_title: Second Labour MP suspended over Covid loan repayments

sentences.text: "We cannot comment further while the investigation is ongoing." This is the second investigation the Labour Party has launched into the loans, with Alaba, the MP for Southend East and Rochford , also referring himself for investigation over loans made to a real estate company, Alaba Properties.
sentences.article_title: Second Labour MP suspended over Covid loan repayments

sentences.text: At the time, Alaba said: "There has been no attempt to avoid my financial obligations, and I am wholeheartedly committed to ensuring that the liability is met in full." McMurdock, who now sits as an independent, was the first MP to be questioned over bounce back loans given to two fitness companies worth £70,000.
sentences.article_title: Second Labour MP suspended over Covid loan repayments

sentences.text: In 2025 McMurdock said all his business dealings had been compliant with the rules, adding that after taking "specialist legal advice" he had decided "to continue my parliamentary career as an independent MP".
sentences.article_title: Second Labour MP suspended over Covid loan repayments

sentences.text: Alice Webb died after becoming unwell following a liquid Brazilian Butt Lift procedure Only properly trained professionals will be allowed to offer high-risk cosmetic procedures like liquid Brazilian butt lifts (BBLs), vampire facials and chemical peels, under long-awaited government plans for England in 2027.
sentences.article_title: Tighter rules planned to protect people from cosmetic surgery that goes badly wrong

sentences.text: The government said it wanted to "drive cosmetic cowboys out of the market" and shield people from treatments "that can go badly wrong".
sentences.article_title: Tighter rules planned to protect people from cosmetic surgery that goes badly wrong

sentences.text: Currently, there are no restrictions over who can carry out these 'no scalpel' procedures, which can harm or kill if not performed safely.
sentences.article_title: Tighter rules planned to protect people from cosmetic surgery that goes badly wrong

sentences.text: Under the new rules, high-risk procedures for under-18s will also be banned, and rogue providers will face new criminal offences and fixed fines of up to £4,000.
sentences.article_title: Tighter rules planned to protect people from cosmetic surgery that goes badly wrong

sentences.text: Sasha Dean from Bedfordshire was left in a coma after receiving a liquid BBL The government began consulting on changes to the cosmetic surgery industry in 2023, but there have been calls for stricter regulations for many years.
sentences.article_title: Tighter rules planned to protect people from cosmetic surgery that goes badly wrong

sentences.text: It comes following horror stories of procedures reportedly carried out in Airbnbs, hotel rooms, garden sheds and even public toilets, by "cosmetic cowboys" , external .
sentences.article_title: Tighter rules planned to protect people from cosmetic surgery that goes badly wrong

sentences.text: Women have told the BBC of dangerous complications , pain and permanent scarring after treatment by rogue operators.
sentences.article_title: Tighter rules planned to protect people from cosmetic surgery that goes badly wrong

sentences.text: Alice Webb, a mother-of-five from Gloucestershire, died within hours of getting a liquid Brazilian butt lift in 2024.
sentences.article_title: Tighter rules planned to protect people from cosmetic surgery that goes badly wrong

sentences.text: That same year, Sasha Dean, from Bedfordshire, was left in a coma after receiving a liquid BBL.
sentences.article_title: Tighter rules planned to protect people from cosmetic surgery that goes badly wrong

sentences.text: A BBL is a non-surgical cosmetic procedure in which dermal fillers are injected into the buttocks to alter their size or shape.
sentences.article_title: Tighter rules planned to protect people from cosmetic surgery that goes badly wrong

sentences.text: Some of Sasha's treatment took place in a private house and she ended up developing sepsis.
sentences.article_title: Tighter rules planned to protect people from cosmetic surgery that goes badly wrong

sentences.text: She told BBC News: "Very quickly it turned into a complete nightmare.
sentences.article_title: Tighter rules planned to protect people from cosmetic surgery that goes badly wrong

sentences.text: "I had a heart attack, one of my lungs had collapsed, my kidneys were failing.
sentences.article_title: Tighter rules planned to protect people from cosmetic surgery that goes badly wrong

sentences.text: But Mr Keith Allison, from the Royal College of Surgeons of England, said the consultation was "long overdue" and, while welcome, the proposals did not go far enough.
sentences.article_title: Tighter rules planned to protect people from cosmetic surgery that goes badly wrong

sentences.text: "Ministers must ensure they do not create a new loophole in patient protection by regulating non-surgical cosmetic procedures more robustly than cosmetic surgery itself.
sentences.article_title: Tighter rules planned to protect people from cosmetic surgery that goes badly wrong

sentences.text: "A doctor should not be able to carry out cosmetic surgery simply because they hold a medical license." The government will now ask , external doctors, businesses, regulators, the public and other experts for their say on the draft rules, before plans go through parliament in  spring 2027.
sentences.article_title: Tighter rules planned to protect people from cosmetic surgery that goes badly wrong

sentences.text: A licensing scheme for Botox clinics in England to improve safety standards has already been announced.
sentences.article_title: Tighter rules planned to protect people from cosmetic surgery that goes badly wrong

sentences.text: In Scotland, laws passed in March mean cosmetic procedures must be performed by, or alongside, certain healthcare professionals in a registered setting.
sentences.article_title: Tighter rules planned to protect people from cosmetic surgery that goes badly wrong

sentences.text: Non-surgical procedures are banned for under 18s.
sentences.article_title: Tighter rules planned to protect people from cosmetic surgery that goes badly wrong

sentences.text: There are no dedicated regulations around cosmetic procedures in Wales or Northern Ireland.
sentences.article_title: Tighter rules planned to protect people from cosmetic surgery that goes badly wrong

sentences.text: This video can not be played 'We're very busy' - inside Wales' newest hospital It is the £350m "super hospital" that has been slammed as "dangerous" and a "disgrace" on social media.
sentences.article_title: On frontline at hospital denying online claims it is 'dangerous' and 'dreadful'

sentences.text: At just six years old, the Grange University Hospital in Cwmbran has already come under fire for long delays, overcrowding, staff shortages and the quality of its care.
sentences.article_title: On frontline at hospital denying online claims it is 'dangerous' and 'dreadful'

sentences.text: But senior staff insist it's one of the safest in Wales on patient safety and survival rates.
sentences.article_title: On frontline at hospital denying online claims it is 'dangerous' and 'dreadful'

sentences.text: BBC Wales spent the day on the frontline at the hospital as 999 calls came in.
sentences.article_title: On frontline at hospital denying online claims it is 'dangerous' and 'dreadful'

sentences.text: The Grange has arguably the best view of any hospital in Wales The PA announcement in A&E is clear, somebody's life is in danger and they'll soon be arriving by ambulance.
sentences.article_title: On frontline at hospital denying online claims it is 'dangerous' and 'dreadful'

sentences.text: But all eight beds at the Emergency Department's (ED) resuscitation unit, where the sickest patients go, are already full.
sentences.article_title: On frontline at hospital denying online claims it is 'dangerous' and 'dreadful'

sentences.text: Staff have to decide quickly which patient to move.
sentences.article_title: On frontline at hospital denying online claims it is 'dangerous' and 'dreadful'

sentences.text: But two similar "crash calls" have already come in by ambulance, as well as someone who walked into an already-full reception having a suspected heart attack.
sentences.article_title: On frontline at hospital denying online claims it is 'dangerous' and 'dreadful'

sentences.text: Overall there are more than 90 patients in the department with the longest wait about 18 hours.
sentences.article_title: On frontline at hospital denying online claims it is 'dangerous' and 'dreadful'

sentences.text: Medical staff in resus swarm a patient supported by an Air Ambulance crew "We're currently over capacity," says Dr Zoe Morgan-Pittard, who is so busy that she's placed stickers on her arms to remind her who she's been assessing.
sentences.article_title: On frontline at hospital denying online claims it is 'dangerous' and 'dreadful'

sentences.text: "We've had to move three patients already who probably aren't well enough.
sentences.article_title: On frontline at hospital denying online claims it is 'dangerous' and 'dreadful'

sentences.text: "But the sickest patients have to take priority, we're having to make fluid decisions.
sentences.article_title: On frontline at hospital denying online claims it is 'dangerous' and 'dreadful'

sentences.article_title: On frontline at hospital denying online claims it is 'dangerous' and 'dreadful'
