sentences.text: Mindy says people often presume she is straight because of her age As a 75-year-old lesbian, Mindy Meleyal has lived through every major milestone in the modern LGBT rights movement, from the start of decriminalisation in 1967 to the first same-sex marriages in 2014.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: But now she says this important part of her identity is frequently overlooked due to her age.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: She's part of England's older LGBTQ+ community, which a new report suggests often experiences poorer health, more limited finances and greater social isolation than the wider older population.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: The report, from the Centre for Ageing Better, says without specialist support, this growing demographic could be forced "back into the closet" when accessing care, warning they may even delay getting the care they need because of concerns about homophobia.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: Adam Preston, a housing development manager from the LGBT Foundation charity, says he regularly meets older members of the community in exactly that situation.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: "It's very common for people to hide things if they have a carer visiting their home, for example hiding their wedding photos or taking down a trans flag," he says.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: Preston is part of the team behind Kindred House, a first-of-its-kind LGBTQ+ social housing scheme for over-55s, set to open in Manchester next year.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: An artist's impression of what Kindred House will look like when it opens The scheme, a joint project with the local council, will provide 80 self-contained apartments and communal areas available to the local community.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: The majority of residents will be LGBTQ+.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: The Kindred House scheme is what's known as extra-care housing, which means residents live independently, but there is a 24/7 care team available for those who need extra help, and all staff will receive specialist training around LGBTQ+ inclusion.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: Preston says he hopes the scheme will "trigger some conversations" about how to best support older LGBTQ+ people in the challenges they face.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: Mindy and her wife Linda have been together for more than 30 years, but says they're often mistaken for sisters.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: "She's 18 inches taller than me, I've got a Yorkshire accent and she's got a Northern Irish accent," Mindy says.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: "I think it's pretty obvious we weren't brought up in the same building." She believes part of that is often down to people presuming she is straight because of her age.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: "There are different tribes of people in every age group, but when you get older, people start clumping you together with other stereotypes," she says.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Nearly 90,000 doses of the vaccine have already been given, with 135,000 more booked in for the coming weeks.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: So who needs the vaccine, what's in it and where can you get it for free?
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: The vaccine offers protection against a dangerous strain of meningitis called meningitis B (MenB) that caused the outbreak in Kent.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: The vaccine does not contain any live bacteria and cannot cause meningitis.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: It is common to get some swelling, redness or tenderness where you have the injection.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: You may also get a mild fever, nausea, headache or muscle aches but these symptoms should disappear after one or two days.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: More serious side effects are rare.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Bookings can be made at high street pharmacies across England.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Seventeen and 18-year-olds can book via the NHS National Booking Service , external if they are already registered with a GP , external .
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Other students under the age of 25 who are heading to a residential college or university this autumn for the first time can also contact a participating pharmacy.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: You do not need to be registered with a GP surgery to use the walk-in service.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Find a participating pharmacy here , external .
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: The vaccine, given as two doses and at least 28 days apart, is being offered to 17 and 18-year-olds in sixth form and students under the age of 25 who are heading to a residential college or university this autumn for the first time.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Both doses are needed for the fullest protection.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Within weeks, in Kent, there were 29 confirmed or suspected cases and two deaths.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: That's why the new, one-off campaign is being launched - to help protect those at greatest risk and hopefully prevent something like this from happening again.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Students in their first year of university have a risk that is about seven times higher than that of young people of a similar age who do not go to university, says NHS England.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Meningitis infections can be spread through close contact - for example through kissing, sharing vapes and drinks or living in close quarters with a person with the bug.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: UK health officials say the risk to 18-year-olds or those entering university or a residential college for the first time is higher because of increased mixing of social groups and shared accommodation.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: MenB infection can cause serious, life-threatening problems including inflammation of the lining of the brain (meningitis) and blood poisoning (sepsis).
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: It can lead to life-changing disabilities such as amputations, hearing loss and brain damage, and in some cases can be fatal.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Vaccination can save lives.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: The MenB vaccine was added to the UK NHS childhood immunisation programme for babies born on or after 1 July 2015.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: All babies are now offered it.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: But it means teenagers and young adults over the age of 11 have not received this jab.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Young babies are vaccinated because they are more likely to get invasive infections more often than other age groups, and their bodies are less likely to be able to fight them off.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: However, research suggests the MenB vaccine doesn't necessarily prevent transmission of the infection from person to person, doesn't target all the different B bacteria strains and doesn't provide long-term protection.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: But UK vaccine experts now say government should consider routinely offering the vaccine to all teenagers at around age 15 .
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: It will be up to ministers in each nation to decide whether to do this.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Meanwhile, they do want everyone who is eligible to come forward and get the vaccine because it can prevent serious illness.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Around 10,000 people in the Kent region will have already received jabs, as part of the response to the March outbreak.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Each nation has its own plans , external , but all are offering the vaccine to most pupils completing Year 13 or S6 in the summer of 2026 - irrespective of their education plans and including people from this age group who are not currently in school.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Young people aged 18-25 starting university or moving into residential further education settings for the first time in autumn 2026 are also eligible.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: In Wales, those aged 17-18 will receive a letter invite, while those aged 18-25 who are entering higher education will need to contact their health board later in July.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Meningitis can be caused by many different types of viruses or bacteria, which are spread through close contact with a person who has them.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Viral meningitis tends to get better on its own within seven to 10 days.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: It can often be treated at home with plenty of rest, painkillers and anti-sickness medicine.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Bacterial meningitis needs to be treated in hospital.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Outbreaks are thankfully rare.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Currently, a separate vaccine covering different strains, the MenACWY vaccine, is offered routinely to 14-year-olds.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Franklin was a British chemist and crystallographer, whose X-ray diffraction work helped discover the structure of DNA Rosalind Franklin is the only female scientist named in GCSE and National 5 science exam specifications in the UK, according to new research.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: A Cambridge study found that of the 86 scientists named by UK exam boards, the English chemist, whose work in the 1950s helped reveal the structure of DNA, was the only woman.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: Exam specifications set out the skills and knowledge students are expected to have gained by the end of their course and how they will be assessed.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: Exam boards said there was "a clear need for greater representation in science qualifications".
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: Academics from the University of Cambridge, along with institutions in the US and Australia, examined how many women were mentioned in specifications for biology, chemistry, physics, environmental science, geology and astronomy.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: Their work, published in the British Educational Research Journal, looked at six exam boards in the UK: At Key Stage 4 and equivalent, including GCSEs and National 5s in Scotland, Franklin was the only woman among the 86 scientists mentioned.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: She was also one of three women mentioned at Key Stage 5 and equivalent - including A-levels, AS-levels, National Highers and National Advanced Highers - out of a total of 181 scientists.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: Marie Tharp, an American cartographer who created the first map of the floor of the Atlantic ocean in the 1950s, and Inge Lehmann, a Danish seismologist who discovered the existence of the Earth's inner core in the 1930s, both feature in the Cambridge OCR's A-­level Geology.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: Franklin, who was named in Cambridge OCR's GCSE Biology and Scottish Highers Biology, produced a famous DNA image known as Photograph 51.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: Cambridge scientists Francis Crick and James Watson used the image to work out the following year that DNA has a double-helix structure.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: Watson, Crick and Franklin's colleague Maurice Wilkins received the 1962 Nobel Prize for the discovery.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: Franklin had died four years earlier.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: Academics who wrote the paper found that "several major scientific breakthroughs" in specifications were made by women, but they were not explicitly mentioned.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: The paper said: "Many of the scientific discoveries and explanations were developed in the 1800s and early 1900s, a period when scientific and mathematical practice was largely, but not solely, dominated by men.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: "Our findings confirm that the UK science specifications reflect this historical imbalance: although women made significant contributions to major scientific breakthroughs, this fact is rarely acknowledged." The academics recommended that Franklin should be included "in all specifications when teaching DNA structure".
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: They also said specifications should refer to Marie Curie, who discovered radium and polonium and coined the term radioactivity, and nuclear physicist Lise Meitner, who discovered nuclear fission, among others.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: The Department for Education in England said "girls should see the contribution women have made in STEM", adding it was "committed to improving the school curriculum over the coming years, and as part of that will make sure every girl can see where their learning can take them".
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: The Scottish Government said it was "committed to closing the gender gap in STEM and will carefully consider the findings of this research".
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: As temperatures exceed 30C (86F) in some parts of the UK this week, the last thing people want to do is turn on the oven.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Not only can cooking in hot weather feel like a chore, but many of us find ourselves feeling less hungry altogether.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: So when the heat gets too much, should we consider changing our diet?
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Here are three things to think about next time you're hot and hungry.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Cooking chicken in an air fryer uses less than half the energy of a conventional oven "There's no need for more protein in a heatwave," says Aisling Daly, senior lecturer in nutrition at Oxford Brookes University.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: But if you fancy it, some of the most common proteins will need cooking (like meat, chicken and fish) and that can be off-putting in the heat.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Even an outdoor BBQ can be too hot to handle.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Cooking a chicken leg in the worktop device uses less than half the energy of a conventional oven, according to Radio 4's Sliced Bread .
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: And because they are smaller and speedier, they also pump less heat into your kitchen.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: But experts say don't forget about your slightly less fashionable slow cooker - likely buried in the back of your cupboard.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Even though they run for longer, they're typically more energy efficient and release even less heat than the air fryer.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: The reality, though, is that simply by eating and digesting protein, our bodies produce more heat than other food groups.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: That's due to the energy needed by the stomach, intestines and liver to break down and absorb these complex molecules.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: So that steak you crave will only bring you out in a sweat.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: But you can also get your protein from lentils, nuts, milk, tofu and cheese too.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: To reduce body heat while still getting your protein fix, Dr Daly recommends focusing on things like bean salads, eggs, pre-cooked meats and plenty of Greek yoghurt (frozen too).
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Making a smoothie by blending up fruit, veg and yogurt (while adding in peanut butter for protein) can provide a balanced, nutritious meal in an easy way.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: And it might also be time to turn to some lighter fish, such as tuna, salmon or prawns.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: When it's hot, we lose water when we sweat, so we need to replace it or we become dehydrated.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Six to eight glasses of fluid a day is normally recommended by the NHS, , external and in a heatwave you could need a lot more.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: "There is no single amount that suits everyone, because how much fluid your body needs depends on lots of factors like your age, body size, activity levels and health status," says Dr Charlotte Mills, food and nutrition scientist at the University of Reading.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: World Cup footballers aren't the only ones who benefit from hydration breaks: other athletes and pregnant and breastfeeding women are among those who need to drink more.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: But rehydrating doesn't just mean refilling your water bottle every couple of hours.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: "We need to eat our water as well as drink it," says Dr Daly, "80-90% of fruit and vegetables are full of water." Cucumber, tomatoes, lettuce, celery, watermelon and strawberries all have very high water content, above 90%.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Apples, carrots, cooked broccoli and pears contain 80% to 89% water, as do oranges, grapes and pineapple.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: In comparison, boiled eggs are 75% water , external , with digestive biscuits only 2.8% water , external .
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Even a cheese and tomato pizza is 38% water, with takeaway chips containing as much as 51%.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: If your mouth has dried up just reading this, try some of these water-rich recipes .
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: A useful way to check if you're hydrated is to check the colour of your urine.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Pale yellow is what you're after.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: If it's orangey or dark brown, that's a sign that your kidneys - which filter waste products and produce urine - are holding onto water because there isn't enough in the body.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: That means you're dehydrated and need to drink more.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Warm or room-temperature drinks are just as good as cold ones for cooling you down We know some people love a cuppa, even when it's sweltering, and that actually makes scientific sense.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Warm or room-temperature drinks are just as good as cold ones for cooling you down, says Dr Daly.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Research suggests your body sweats more quickly to get rid of the excess heat after a hot drink.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: After a cold drink, your body sweats more slowly.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Your body is trying to keep your core temperature steady at about 37 degrees celsius.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: So hot tea won't necessarily help you cool down more quickly - the key thing is to stay hydrated no matter the temperature of the liquid.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: You don't need to shun your favourite coffee either just because it's hot - although too much caffeine can make the body produce more urine, and leave you dehydrated.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: For matcha fans, the drink contains more caffeine than a cup of tea but less than a regular coffee.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Dr Daly says one or two coffees a day should make little difference to your hydration levels - but five or six will start to have an effect.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Bear in mind that drinking alcohol also dehydrates.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: You could structure your day differently too, and take a southern European approach to eating.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Have an early breakfast, an afternoon siesta while it's very hot and then a late dinner.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Hayley lost her job as a teaching assistant last October, after being told she was unfit to work Hayley Locksley was 11 years old when she started her periods and excruciating pain became part of her life.
sentences.article_title: I lost my job in a primary school due to endometriosis

sentences.text: "I used to spend every month in the sick room at school," she says.
sentences.article_title: I lost my job in a primary school due to endometriosis

sentences.text: Hayley, from Shefford, Bedfordshire, would often pass out from the pain but the doctors' advice was to take paracetamol.
sentences.article_title: I lost my job in a primary school due to endometriosis

sentences.text: Aged 24, she was diagnosed with endometriosis - a condition that affects one in 10 women, where tissue similar to the lining of the womb grows outside of the uterus.
sentences.article_title: I lost my job in a primary school due to endometriosis

sentences.text: Hayley says she loved her job working in a nursery, but her employers questioned whether her symptoms were real and asked her to use annual leave to cover sick days.
sentences.article_title: I lost my job in a primary school due to endometriosis

sentences.text: After she had surgery for endometriosis, Hayley decided to switch to office work, due to it being less physically demanding.
sentences.article_title: I lost my job in a primary school due to endometriosis

sentences.text: But her new colleagues asked why she was spending so long in the toilet.
sentences.article_title: I lost my job in a primary school due to endometriosis

sentences.text: "I had to explain that my bladder sometimes did not empty fully, causing severe pain and horrendous diarrhoea.
sentences.article_title: I lost my job in a primary school due to endometriosis

sentences.text: I found the questioning embarrassing and humiliating," she says.
sentences.article_title: I lost my job in a primary school due to endometriosis

sentences.text: Hayley had her appendix removed because doctors thought that was the issue, until she was diagnosed with endometriosis After having her daughter, who is now aged seven, Hayley decided to pursue her dream of working with children again and became a special needs teaching assistant in a primary school four years ago.

sentences.article_title: I lost my job in a primary school due to endometriosis

sentences.text: "I didn't want to give up my career but my health meant I could no longer continue," she says.
sentences.article_title: I lost my job in a primary school due to endometriosis

sentences.text: "I now use a walking stick, experience severe back and leg pain, and have fallen numerous times.
sentences.article_title: I lost my job in a primary school due to endometriosis

sentences.text: Losing my job has been so tough for my mental health," she adds.
sentences.article_title: I lost my job in a primary school due to endometriosis

sentences.article_title: I lost my job in a primary school due to endometriosis

sentences.article_title: I lost my job in a primary school due to endometriosis

sentences.article_title: I lost my job in a primary school due to endometriosis

sentences.article_title: I lost my job in a primary school due to endometriosis

sentences.article_title: I lost my job in a primary school due to endometriosis

sentences.article_title: I lost my job in a primary school due to endometriosis

sentences.text: "Having experienced first hand the impact endometriosis can have on your working life, I know just how difficult it can be.

sentences.text: "I really hope this isn't where the conversation ends.

sentences.text: However, to qualify both parents must earn less than £100,000 a year, although all three and four-year-olds are eligible for 15 hours of free childcare, regardless of parental income.

sentences.text: The same £100,000 eligibility threshold also applies to the government's tax-free childcare scheme , external , and has remained unchanged since it was originally set under the Conservative-Liberal Democrat coalition government.

sentences.text: For every £8 paid into an online childcare account, the government adds £2, up to £2,000 per child per year, which parents can then use to pay for childcare.

sentences.text: The Tories said that if they return to power, they would remove the £100,000 threshold entirely for tax-free childcare and government-funded childcare hours.

sentences.text: Ofcom is investigating whether Meta breached its duties under the UK's online safety laws with the launch of its "Instants" feature on Instagram.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: The tool - allowing users to take and share an instant image with close friends, that disappears once viewed - was launched on Meta's photo-sharing app in May as "a new way to share photos in the moment".
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: But the regulator said the social media giant had not properly assessed risks posed by the feature prior to launching it - something it is required to do under the UK's Online Safety Act (OSA).
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: A Meta spokesperson said in a statement that it "takes its regulatory obligations under the Online Safety Act seriously".
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: "We conducted a risk analysis and briefed Ofcom about this feature on a number of occasions before launching it," they said.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: "We will of course co-operate with Ofcom during this investigation." Ofcom said its probe would examine whether Meta breached OSA duties by not carrying out "a suitable and sufficient illegal content risk assessment and children's risk assessment before the launch of Instants".
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: Under the UK's sweeping online safety rules, platforms including Meta must carry out and update risk assessments to comply with a range of duties, including to tackle illegal content.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: They must also show how they prevent children permitted to use their services from encountering content deemed harmful for them.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: This spans material relating to pornography, or promoting self-harm or suicide - as "priority primary content" - alongside things like abusive, hateful or bullying content.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: "Our online safety laws are clear – significant changes to platforms must be risk assessed before they're launched," said Ofcom enforcement director George Lusty.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: "This is a vital step that tech firms must take to protect their users," he added.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: Images shared with Instants can be viewed by those who have been selected as "close friends" by a user, or those who they follow and are followed back by.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: Meta says the feature has a range of built-in protections, including for younger users with Teen Accounts, including preventing screenshots, reshares or forwarding of Instants.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: But disappearing messages and images have been singled out previously as posing particular risks for child or teen users of some apps .
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: "Safety by design must be built in, not bolted on, and today's investigation shows we'll take action where we have concerns that providers are failing to comply," Lusty added.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: All three companies have appeared in court this week, arguing they should not need to provide so much information in response to Ofcom's formal requests.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: Meta has separately also argued Ofcom should not be able to levy fines for breaches based on its global annual revenue.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: It also contends that its messaging and image-sharing apps should not have to face additional requirements under the OSA, such as tackling paid-for fraud ads.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: York was the subject of the city-wide pilot, which also put on workshops for parents and offered special training for early years staff.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: Twenty local authorities across England are now signed up to launch similar schemes to tackle the number of pupils starting school without being fully toilet-trained.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: The government said the pilot's results were "encouraging", and confirmed they were committed to 75% of pupils reaching a good level of development at the end of their first year in school by 2028.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: Since April this year, parents across York have been targeted via GP surgeries, pharmacies, family hubs, schools, nurseries and libraries with information and offers of support on how to potty-train their child ahead of starting school.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: Potty training guides were sent out to all families across York who had a child starting reception in September - with the aim that all children could use the toilet independently by the time they started school, except those with medical issues or special educational needs.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: The results from all 55 mainstream primary schools across the city, shared exclusively with BBC News, suggested there had been a 43% drop since last year in the number of children who were not fully toilet-trained when they started school.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: Across York last September, 148 out of 1,364 reception pupils (11%) were recorded as not being toilet-trained when they started school.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: This year, that fell to 85 reception pupils out of 1,374 (6%).
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: Parents Natalie and Lucy, who both have daughters starting reception next year, have welcomed the extra support on offer.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: Mum Natalie says there's a lot of conflicting pressures on parents about the right time to potty-train Lucy said she had noticed the drop-in sessions on potty training in her local children's centre and thought it was a "really good idea".
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: "I think it's really important that children are more prepared for that aspect of starting school," she said.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: Natalie said getting her daughter Freya potty-trained in time for school has been a priority, but feels there is a lot of pressure on parents to do so.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: "I think going to school is hard enough for children," she said.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: "When I was little, we still had the terry towelling nappies and they had to be washed and hung on the line.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: So I think with disposable nappies it's easier," she said.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: Around one in four children started school in England and Wales last year not fully toilet-trained, and teachers said they have been spending over an hour a day changing nappies, according to the latest research from the children's charity Kindred Squared , external .
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: Felicity Gillespie, chief executive of Kindred Squared, told BBC Radio 4's Today programme that children not being potty trained when starting school was "a real concern for teachers".
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: "They tell us that they're losing, on average across the country, a day a week of teaching time to dealing with potty-training issues." Gillespie is keen to spread the message that "it's best for children to be coming out of nappies" when they are between 18 and 30 months old.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: "When the teacher's leaving the class to change someone's nappy, the rest of the class is having their learning broken up.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: So everybody loses out,” she added.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: The ability to listen to and follow instructions is another skill that helps pupils get the most out of learning when they start reception class Jo Mould, who teaches reception at Robert Wilkinson Primary Academy in York, said she has noticed an improvement in pupils being ready for school this year.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: "We've spent more time teaching in these last three weeks than we have in previous years," she said.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: "The children have come in so ready to learn, because they're more settled and regulated socially and emotionally.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: We've had a really, really positive start to the school year." Jo Mould says not having to deal with toilet training has meant more time spent teaching her pupils York councillor Bob Webb said the impact of the scheme had been "so positive" for both schools and families.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: But he acknowledged a potential "gap in support" for parents between seeing health visitors with their toddler, and the child later arriving at school.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: He said the key to the scheme's success was collaboration across health visitors, schools and other community settings, but that there was "always more that could be done at an earlier age".
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: Twenty local authorities across England have now committed to adopt York's model, developed by Kindred Squared, and use it to encourage earlier potty-training in their areas.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: That means they were assessed by teachers on being able to complete tasks like going to the toilet and paying attention in class.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: The government has said it is still committed to increasing that proportion to 75% by 2028.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: Early Education Minister Paul Waugh said it was "encouraging to see this pilot helping more children develop the confidence and independence they need before starting school", stressing the importance of parents taking early steps towards toilet training.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: In York, Mould said she hopes next year's parents will take on potty-training even earlier.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: "Ideally we'd be at the point where [children] don't need that support when they get here, because they've already been trained by the time they get to us." Do you have any views, comments or questions about this story?

sentences.text: A woman convinced her former partner she had given birth to two children who most likely did not exist in what a High Court judge described as an "extraordinary" and "elaborate campaign of deceit".
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: The man, who has not been named but was referred to as John in the judgement, applied to the Family Court after he was told the woman had sold their two children for a combined £500.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: The case heard that the man received messages and photos of the children and paid the woman around £30,000 over the course of two years.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: But in a hearing in February, the woman, who was referred to as Jane, told the judge she had lied about the pregnancies for revenge, claiming the man had abused her.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: The court heard the man believed he was the children's' father because in late 2022 his partner told him she was pregnant, sent pictures of an ultrasound image and had become "visibly pregnant" as time went on.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: In May 2023, shortly before the first baby was due, the woman called the police alleging she had been assaulted by the man.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: He was arrested and subsequently held on remand for several months, Mrs Justice Judd said in her ruling which was published on Friday.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: Following this, the woman sent a message to his stepfather saying the baby had been born as well as sharing baby photos.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: At one stage she is said to have sent voice notes to her former partner's mother in the middle of the night with the sound of a baby crying in the background.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: Later, she told the man she was pregnant again and the baby was due in August 2024.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: However, before the due date, the couple split up and did not reconcile.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: The woman would go on to tell the man's mother the baby had been born.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: The woman admitted to the court she had told him she was pregnant when they were together, and afterwards, but conceded she had told a series of elaborate lies and that there were, in fact, no children.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: She argued she was menopausal at the time and could not have been pregnant and bank statements show she attended a tanning shop on the day she said she had given birth, Mrs Justice Judd said.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: In her judgement, the judge concluded that the "factors that weigh against the children genuinely existing were very strong, stronger than the factors pointing the other way".
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: She said the man was the victim of a "sustained and elaborate campaign of deceit" which also impacted his mother and closest friend.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: "Added to this, the behaviour was cruel, leading a man and his mother to believe they had children and grandchildren respectively.", the Judge said.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: The judge added she was unable to conclude the woman's motive for her behaviour but said financial fraud was a "possibility"  and that the "complex mental health problems" she suffered from may have also played a part.

sentences.text: Cases of antisemitism affecting university students and staff in the UK increased in the last academic year, according to a charity that monitors antisemitic incidents.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: The Community Security Trust (CST) said it had recorded 95 "university-related" incidents in the 2025-26 academic year - up from 83 the year before.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: It said the number had fallen from its peak in the year after Hamas attacked Israel on 7 October 2023 and the war in Gaza began, but remains "substantially higher" than before that point.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: Universities UK (UUK) represents more than 140 institutions and said its members needed to "protect Jewish students and staff", adding that the findings were a "serious concern".
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: Lucy Powell, education secretary in England, said the findings in the CST report were "deeply troubling".
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: "We expect universities to take a zero-tolerance approach to antisemitism, and are providing training to help university staff identify and respond to incidents swiftly," she said.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: The CST defines an antisemitic incident as "university-related" if it concerns a student, member of staff or academic at a UK university "in their academic or student capacity" - including on campus and online.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: In 2022-23, the last academic year before the 7 October attack, the CST recorded 53 incidents.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: That grew to 272 in 2023-24.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: A report from the charity examining the past two academic years says reported incidents fell in 2024-25 and but grew again in 2025-26.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: The most common type of incident recorded by CST over both years was abusive behaviour, including verbal abuse, comments made in person or online and antisemitic graffiti.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: Its report said that, for the first time, there were two occurrences of extreme violence in 2024-25.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: It said there were six reported assaults across both years, eight incidents of damage and desecration to Jewish property - five of which were in student accommodation - and ten threats.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: Around two-thirds of reported incidents involved antisemitic language or targeting alongside references to Israel, Gaza, Hamas, the 7 October attack, and the subsequent conflicts in the Middle East.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: The war in Gaza was triggered by the Hamas attack on Israel on 7 October 2023 in which about 1,200 people were killed and 251 others taken hostage.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: Israel launched a mass military offensive on Gaza in response which has killed around 74,000 people, according to the Hamas-run health ministry.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: He added that universities had "a duty to ensure that Jewish students and staff can study, work and participate on campus the same as anyone else".
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: Raphi Leon, president of the Union of Jewish Students, said the report "must be a shot in the arm to boost action to support Jewish students and tackle antisemitism".
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: Vivienne Stern, chief executive of UUK, said: "The rise in antisemitic incidents in the UK, including on university campuses, is a serious concern.

sentences.text: WhatsApp is introducing new parental controls for teenagers, as tech companies continue to come under pressure to provide more age-appropriate experiences for children.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: The social messaging app's new tools will give parents a range of options, such as being told when their child joins or leaves a group.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: It will also let them decide on privacy settings for their account.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: In a blog post, WhatsApp, clarified parents would not be given the power to see the messages their teen is sending and receiving, which along with calls would stay private and protected by end-to-end encryption.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: And it said the controls were optional, which social media analyst Matt Navarra called an "obvious weakness".
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: He said the move was "fairly convenient" for Meta, which owns WhatsApp, because it reduced the company's reliance on age verification by putting some responsibility on parents and teenagers.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: "Meta is trying to show regulators we have a child safety system, we have parental controls and we're rolling it out across our platforms," he said.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: "I think the big unanswered question is whether enough families will actually use it." The minimum age to use WhatsApp is 13 in the UK, although it is higher in some countries.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: According to the firm, parents will be able to adjust or switch off the controls at any time.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: The settings will be "straightforward to set up" using a Pin set by a parent, which teens will need if they want to switch off the controls.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: Some of the new privacy tools include selecting who can see a child's profile photo and who can add them to groups.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: Parents can also choose how their teenager uses Channels, which allows organisations and public figures to send out content.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: And they will have the option of choosing between the default 13+ setting for Meta AI, the app's optional built-in AI assistant, or a stricter "Limited Content" option.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: "All of these controls are being designed to support open conversations about how to use WhatsApp between parents and teens, while keeping everyone's personal messages private," the company said.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: The changes come as pressure mounts on tech companies from governments and regulators to change the way they operate in order to better protect children using their platforms.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: In June, the government announced it plans to ban under-16s from social media platforms, with the restrictions expected to come into force in March 2027.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: It said "highly effective age assurance" measures would be used to check the age of those using social media.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.article_title: Britain's posh schools are heading to India for students and profits

sentences.text: Beyond the growing ranks of well-heeled local families, non-resident Indians who have either returned home after long stints abroad, or those still in the UK or Middle East wanting their children to connect to their roots, are also a significant market for these schools, says Pascoe.
sentences.article_title: Britain's posh schools are heading to India for students and profits

sentences.text: There is also a house system - a hallmark of traditional British education.
sentences.article_title: Britain's posh schools are heading to India for students and profits

sentences.text: These quintessentially parochial quirks are blended with local customs such as singing the Indian national anthem every morning or celebrating Ganesh Chaturthi, a major Hindu festival.
sentences.article_title: Britain's posh schools are heading to India for students and profits

sentences.text: Schools such as Harrow in Bengaluru promote extracurricular activities like music and drama While India's growing economic credentials and burgeoning population of newly minted millionaires are a natural tailwind for expansion, this growth is partly being driven by a slowdown in China.
sentences.article_title: Britain's posh schools are heading to India for students and profits

sentences.text: Much of the expansion of British public schools abroad in the past decade was driven by China and Hong Kong - half of the 151 satellite campuses operated by 50 UK schools are situated in these countries.
sentences.article_title: Britain's posh schools are heading to India for students and profits

sentences.text: But that growth has slowed following changes in regulation, and "increased scrutiny, and even resistance, from national governments", according to a 2025 study by the UK-based Private Education Policy Forum ( PEPF , external ) think tank.
sentences.article_title: Britain's posh schools are heading to India for students and profits

sentences.text: A new 2024 Chinese law that required schools to integrate patriotic education into all subjects further challenged expansion and even led to planned campuses being cancelled, prompting these schools to consider other locations like India and Vietnam, according to PEPF.
sentences.article_title: Britain's posh schools are heading to India for students and profits

sentences.text: Moreover, in the 2024 Autumn Budget, Britain introduced a 20% VAT on private school fees.
sentences.article_title: Britain's posh schools are heading to India for students and profits

sentences.text: Naomi Atkins, founding principal at Bedford School Mohali, says this has forced many private schools to look overseas.
sentences.article_title: Britain's posh schools are heading to India for students and profits

sentences.text: "They are in a desperate situation.
sentences.article_title: Britain's posh schools are heading to India for students and profits

sentences.text: Even those that hadn't previously looked for international expansion are now suddenly active in India," she told the BBC.
sentences.article_title: Britain's posh schools are heading to India for students and profits

sentences.text: Well-heeled local families and non-resident Indians are a major target market for British schools in India But India has not been an easy market, she admits.
sentences.article_title: Britain's posh schools are heading to India for students and profits

sentences.text: Most of these schools are set up in partnership with local investors or operators.
sentences.article_title: Britain's posh schools are heading to India for students and profits

sentences.text: While in the past schools in other countries might have been able to do deals at 10% of revenue - the fee that they would charge the local partner-investor - margins in India may have shrunk to as low as 1% in some cases, says Atikins.
sentences.article_title: Britain's posh schools are heading to India for students and profits

sentences.text: There has also been some over-estimation of the size of the market, she says.
sentences.article_title: Britain's posh schools are heading to India for students and profits

sentences.text: Even though India has nearly 250 million children enrolled in schools, English education is deeply entrenched in the country and competition from local players is much more intense compared with other non-English speaking countries like China, Korea or Vietnam.
sentences.article_title: Britain's posh schools are heading to India for students and profits

sentences.text: India's per capita income is also far lower and the high price-points of the British schools - which can charge up to £15,000 or more for full boarding - can limit growth.
sentences.article_title: Britain's posh schools are heading to India for students and profits

sentences.text: "I've worked in Indonesia, Malaysia and China but Indians are much more price-sensitive - they like a bargain," says Atkins.
sentences.article_title: Britain's posh schools are heading to India for students and profits

sentences.text: That is why Bedford Mohali has set its fees at roughly half those charged by other British schools.
sentences.article_title: Britain's posh schools are heading to India for students and profits

sentences.text: Between 2011-12 and 2022-23, the satellite campuses of British schools generated £152.4m in profit, according to PEPF, and this profit has grown substantially over the years.
sentences.article_title: Britain's posh schools are heading to India for students and profits

sentences.text: But in India, it appears growth is likely to be slow and steady rather than explosive.
sentences.article_title: Britain's posh schools are heading to India for students and profits

sentences.text: The country's old colonial roots and new money afford the legacy institutions a significant business opportunity, but it is unlikely to be big enough to offset the loss of the Chinese market, at least immediately.
sentences.article_title: Britain's posh schools are heading to India for students and profits

sentences.text: Cara is hoping to raise her grade by sitting more Maths GCSE exams in Year 12 There have been calls to pause changes to GCSE Maths which will lead to many exams taken in November each year being scrapped.
sentences.article_title: Changes to GCSE Maths 'pulling the rug out from under pupils'

sentences.text: From 2027, students will only be able to take their exam in November if they are re-sitting the subject.
sentences.article_title: Changes to GCSE Maths 'pulling the rug out from under pupils'

sentences.text: One head of maths in a County Tyrone school said that was "pulling the rug out from under pupils who need those structured manageable steps to succeed".
sentences.article_title: Changes to GCSE Maths 'pulling the rug out from under pupils'

sentences.text: But the Department of Education (DE) said that schools had been given "sufficient notice to plan for the revised arrangements".
sentences.article_title: Changes to GCSE Maths 'pulling the rug out from under pupils'

sentences.text: In some schools, pupils take their Maths GCSE exams in stages throughout the course, using a staggered approach.
sentences.article_title: Changes to GCSE Maths 'pulling the rug out from under pupils'

sentences.text: For example, at Dean Maguirc College in County Tyrone pupils sit some exams in November and summer of year 11.
sentences.article_title: Changes to GCSE Maths 'pulling the rug out from under pupils'

sentences.text: That gives them a GCSE grade which they can increase by sitting more maths exams in year 12.
sentences.article_title: Changes to GCSE Maths 'pulling the rug out from under pupils'

sentences.text: But from 2027, they will not be able to do that anymore as the November exams will only be for students who have finished their GCSE Maths course and want to re-sit the subject.
sentences.article_title: Changes to GCSE Maths 'pulling the rug out from under pupils'

sentences.text: The decision has been taken by the Council for the Curriculum, Examinations and Assessment (CCEA) exam board and DE.
sentences.article_title: Changes to GCSE Maths 'pulling the rug out from under pupils'

sentences.text: Spacing out exams allows for extra revision, Maeve says At Dean Maguirc College, an all-ability school, 15-year-old Maeve said maths was a vital subject to learn.
sentences.article_title: Changes to GCSE Maths 'pulling the rug out from under pupils'

sentences.text: "It's to do with everyday life and you need it for loads of stuff like money and most jobs," she said.
sentences.article_title: Changes to GCSE Maths 'pulling the rug out from under pupils'

sentences.text: She said that being able to sit some of her maths exams in November gave her more time to revise for her other GCSEs in the summer.
sentences.article_title: Changes to GCSE Maths 'pulling the rug out from under pupils'

sentences.text: "They're not all crammed together," she said.
sentences.article_title: Changes to GCSE Maths 'pulling the rug out from under pupils'

sentences.text: "For maths, like, there's a lot of stuff to learn so when you have the one exam to do in November you can learn all of that for November, you don't have to keep looking over it until summertime." Maeve said that, in her opinion, the decision was "not fair".
sentences.article_title: Changes to GCSE Maths 'pulling the rug out from under pupils'

sentences.text: The changes are set to come into effect next year Fifteen-year-old Cara is also currently studying maths for GCSE at Dean Maguirc College and she also has concerns.
sentences.article_title: Changes to GCSE Maths 'pulling the rug out from under pupils'

sentences.text: "Getting half of your exam done with in November I found it really eased the pressure," she said.
sentences.article_title: Changes to GCSE Maths 'pulling the rug out from under pupils'

sentences.text: "And it allowed me to focus half of my subject into June." As she had achieved a C-star grade by the end of year 11, she is hoping to make her grade higher by sitting more maths GCSE exams in year 12.
sentences.article_title: Changes to GCSE Maths 'pulling the rug out from under pupils'

sentences.text: She said that being able to divide the maths exams up and take them in stages benefitted everyone and is worried about the impact of the changes.
sentences.article_title: Changes to GCSE Maths 'pulling the rug out from under pupils'

sentences.text: "I think it's unfair and gives less of an opportunity for the people upcoming," she said.
sentences.article_title: Changes to GCSE Maths 'pulling the rug out from under pupils'

sentences.text: "I did struggle at maths when I was younger," he said.
sentences.article_title: Changes to GCSE Maths 'pulling the rug out from under pupils'

sentences.text: "It feels like CCEA are pulling down a ladder that helped students like me climb higher, because not all students are able to do it in one go and instead have to do it step by step.
sentences.article_title: Changes to GCSE Maths 'pulling the rug out from under pupils'

sentences.text: "So they can gradually reach their full potential." Máire McGinn is head of maths at Dean Maguirc College and had previously served on Northern Ireland's literacy and numeracy task force.
sentences.article_title: Changes to GCSE Maths 'pulling the rug out from under pupils'

sentences.text: "Maths is everywhere and it underpins everything that a pupil is going to need to get through their future life," she said.
sentences.article_title: Changes to GCSE Maths 'pulling the rug out from under pupils'

sentences.text: "It provides manageable milestones for pupils, structuring it like that," McGinn said.
sentences.article_title: Changes to GCSE Maths 'pulling the rug out from under pupils'

sentences.text: She said CCEA was "pulling the rug out from under pupils who need those structured manageable steps to succeed".
sentences.article_title: Changes to GCSE Maths 'pulling the rug out from under pupils'

sentences.text: Many other maths teachers across Northern Ireland also felt that "this policy change is not in our pupils best interests", she added.
sentences.article_title: Changes to GCSE Maths 'pulling the rug out from under pupils'

sentences.text: "I would ask CCEA to pause what they have suggested is going to happen and consult with teachers." A DE spokesperson said: "The decision to change the November CCEA GCSE Mathematics examination series to a resit-only series from 2027 was an operational decision taken by CCEA.
sentences.article_title: Changes to GCSE Maths 'pulling the rug out from under pupils'

sentences.text: "CCEA has advised the department that the decision followed consideration of a range of educational factors, including the impact of assessment arrangements on pupils' learning and on teaching time in schools.
sentences.article_title: Changes to GCSE Maths 'pulling the rug out from under pupils'

sentences.text: "CCEA's Maths GCSE will continue to be a modular qualification with pupils able to sit modules at the end of Year 11 as well as the end of Year 12.
sentences.article_title: Changes to GCSE Maths 'pulling the rug out from under pupils'

sentences.text: "The November series will remain available for pupils who have completed the qualification and wish to improve their grade." The changes will apply from 2027, "providing schools with sufficient notice to plan for the revised arrangements".
sentences.article_title: Changes to GCSE Maths 'pulling the rug out from under pupils'
