sentences.text: George McMaster uses technology to help him with work on his farm George McMaster's farming career started with milking eight cows in a byre, relying on his eyes to spot any health issues in his cattle.
sentences.article_title: From agriculture to AI-griculture: How tech is changing farming

sentences.text: He still watches his now-300-strong herd, but via a feed from an AI camera in the milking parlour at the farm near Islandmagee in County Antrim.
sentences.article_title: From agriculture to AI-griculture: How tech is changing farming

sentences.text: The device uses an algorithm which assigns each cow its own ID, records a short video of the animal every day, analyses it and flags any changes - often before they are visible to the human eye.
sentences.article_title: From agriculture to AI-griculture: How tech is changing farming

sentences.text: For the third generation farmer, it is "absolutely incredible to move from all hand-done to sitting on the phone, watching what's happening outside".
sentences.article_title: From agriculture to AI-griculture: How tech is changing farming

sentences.text: Jack and his father George on their Islandmagee farm It is just one example of how technology is changing the traditional profession.
sentences.article_title: From agriculture to AI-griculture: How tech is changing farming

sentences.text: George's son Jack, who is taking over the farm, jumped at the chance to get involved with the CattleEye app when a local developer approached him.
sentences.article_title: From agriculture to AI-griculture: How tech is changing farming

sentences.text: He, too, is astonished by the potential.
sentences.article_title: From agriculture to AI-griculture: How tech is changing farming

sentences.text: "There's cows there we would never have thought of as lame when we were just watching them every day, but whenever the camera's watching they're picking them up so much earlier, any emergencies that we have, to check cows before they lose condition and get sick," he said.
sentences.article_title: From agriculture to AI-griculture: How tech is changing farming

sentences.text: "And if cows are in better health, we get more milk and they're happier - happy cows make happy farmers." AI is helping farmers monitor the health of their herds Caleb Howard is using technology to manage his 90 Jersey cows on the farm near Coagh in County Tyrone.
sentences.article_title: From agriculture to AI-griculture: How tech is changing farming

sentences.text: They filter in and out of a robotic milking machine when they want to, rather than being herded in at set times.
sentences.article_title: From agriculture to AI-griculture: How tech is changing farming

sentences.text: Like the McMasters, he thinks "everything is going down the robotic route" to improve efficiency.
sentences.article_title: From agriculture to AI-griculture: How tech is changing farming

sentences.text: But historically in a place like rural Tyrone, that has come with its own challenges.
sentences.article_title: From agriculture to AI-griculture: How tech is changing farming

sentences.text: Getting high-speed broadband was a game-changer for him - he has been able to open a farm shop with an electronic payment system.
sentences.article_title: From agriculture to AI-griculture: How tech is changing farming

sentences.text: Caleb Howard is a farmer in County Tyrone "Ten years ago, in our area, phone signal was rubbish, the broadband wasn't great, it was just like a slightly faster dial-up," he said.
sentences.article_title: From agriculture to AI-griculture: How tech is changing farming

sentences.text: "So now everything is much simpler and much easier-used when you've got a good internet connection." Project Stratum was set up to deliver high-speed broadband to areas like the one Howard lives in.
sentences.article_title: From agriculture to AI-griculture: How tech is changing farming

sentences.text: Colin Hutchinson from Fibrus, which delivered the project, said it had had a "massive" economic impact.
sentences.article_title: From agriculture to AI-griculture: How tech is changing farming

sentences.text: "Being online and having good broadband access is really crucial now," he said.
sentences.article_title: From agriculture to AI-griculture: How tech is changing farming

sentences.text: "And it's enabling businesses like this to thrive in really rural locations." A milking machine screen is used on Caleb Howard's farm Robert Smyth runs a herd of 100 dairy cows in another rural location, near Randalstown in County Antrim.
sentences.article_title: From agriculture to AI-griculture: How tech is changing farming

sentences.text: For four years now, he has used the FarmDrive app to run the business.
sentences.article_title: From agriculture to AI-griculture: How tech is changing farming

sentences.text: "It's so much handier - beforehand you're writing things down, bits of paperwork in the cattle house and writing them down in the office, whereas now you just do it at that time," he said.
sentences.article_title: From agriculture to AI-griculture: How tech is changing farming

sentences.text: "And then whenever you have inspections coming up, all you have to do is go into your compliance section, select reports, and there's your reports for your medicine, for your meal records, for everything.
sentences.article_title: From agriculture to AI-griculture: How tech is changing farming

sentences.text: "The AI really should be looking towards how to manage your farm better and how to reduce your inputs and increase your outputs." Gareth McDonald developed the FarmDrive app Developer Gareth McDonald describes FarmDrive as "Facebook for cows".
sentences.article_title: From agriculture to AI-griculture: How tech is changing farming

sentences.text: Each animal gets a profile with all her records in one place and a photo can be added.
sentences.article_title: From agriculture to AI-griculture: How tech is changing farming

sentences.text: He comes from a farming background and studied computer science.
sentences.article_title: From agriculture to AI-griculture: How tech is changing farming

sentences.text: Although he is passionate about the technology, he does not believe it will replace humans.
sentences.article_title: From agriculture to AI-griculture: How tech is changing farming

sentences.text: "It's allowing us to work a lot more quickly and efficiently, and on the farming side, it's basically allowing the farmer to see the right information at the right time, where it's kind of that adviser to the farmer," he said.
sentences.article_title: From agriculture to AI-griculture: How tech is changing farming

sentences.text: "We're very much of the opinion we don't want the AI making the decision for the farmer." Almost a century ago, County Down-born inventor Harry Ferguson transformed the farming industry when he developed the linkage system still used in tractors today.

sentences.text: Former president of the Ulster Farmers' Union Ian Marshall says AI is similarly revolutionary.
sentences.article_title: From agriculture to AI-griculture: How tech is changing farming

sentences.text: While the industry has always relied on data, he believes technology will drive how information is used.
sentences.article_title: From agriculture to AI-griculture: How tech is changing farming

sentences.text: "When we take all the datasets, then I think we can deliver on the three pillars of sustainability - economic, environmental and social," he said.

sentences.text: New vocational GCSEs will be introduced from 2029 for 14-year-olds alongside existing core academic subjects in England.
sentences.article_title: Teenagers to be offered new vocational GCSE subjects in school

sentences.text: The new subjects could include building and construction, business management and finance, and child development.
sentences.article_title: Teenagers to be offered new vocational GCSE subjects in school

sentences.text: Education Secretary Lucy Powell said there was "no question" that academic learning was at "the core of any education system", but said there was "huge demand" for subjects with more practical elements too.
sentences.article_title: Teenagers to be offered new vocational GCSE subjects in school

sentences.text: Education unions said the ideas were welcome, but a clear strategy was needed to make them happen.
sentences.article_title: Teenagers to be offered new vocational GCSE subjects in school

sentences.text: The Conservatives said the plans risked "throwing away" progress made in recent years.
sentences.article_title: Teenagers to be offered new vocational GCSE subjects in school

sentences.text: Standards for the new qualifications will be set nationally by the regulator Ofqual to ensure grades are in line with other GCSEs, and will gradually replace other qualifications at this level such as BTec tech awards.
sentences.article_title: Teenagers to be offered new vocational GCSE subjects in school

sentences.text: The vocational GCSEs will be designed to allow teenagers to progress at 16 to studying similar courses at college, including the new V-levels , which schools and colleges are teaching from autumn 2027, and T-levels .
sentences.article_title: Teenagers to be offered new vocational GCSE subjects in school

sentences.text: The idea is to create a clear pathway for teenagers into different types of work through a ladder of qualifications.
sentences.article_title: Teenagers to be offered new vocational GCSE subjects in school

sentences.text: But the Liberal Democrats warned the new vocational GCSEs should not become a "pipeline" directing disadvantaged pupils away from more academic subjects.
sentences.article_title: Teenagers to be offered new vocational GCSE subjects in school

sentences.text: Powell told the BBC she was "not going to oversee a two-tier education system".
sentences.article_title: Teenagers to be offered new vocational GCSE subjects in school

sentences.text: "I want working class, disadvantaged young people to have every opportunity to achieve highly academically," she said.
sentences.article_title: Teenagers to be offered new vocational GCSE subjects in school

sentences.text: Asked whether there would be dedicated funding to help schools cover the cost of the new qualifications, she said the government would "work with the sector to make sure this is absolutely deliverable", and that ministers would "make sure any funding needed is made available".
sentences.article_title: Teenagers to be offered new vocational GCSE subjects in school

sentences.text: A new national target for employers to help create 200,000 work experience opportunities for under-16s is also being set by Prime Minister Andy Burnham, as part of reforms to shake-up the education system to better prepare young people for the world of work.
sentences.article_title: Teenagers to be offered new vocational GCSE subjects in school

sentences.text: Anthony Horan (left) and Ashley Hanley (right) from North East Lincolnshire trace criminals who illegally dump waste A discarded microwave, a mattress sodden by the rain and even a pile of used syringes.

sentences.text: The reality of illegally dumped waste sits before me in a colossal mound next to the side of a motorway.

sentences.text: They tell me it is a goldmine of clues.

sentences.text: "I'm disgusted at the needles.

sentences.article_title: 'It's been relentless' say IT workers on frontline of PHP cyber-security scramble

sentences.text: Other IT and cyber experts have told the BBC about their struggles in the last 48 hours, whose stories give us an insight into what it is like at the coalface of a major cyber emergency.
sentences.article_title: 'It's been relentless' say IT workers on frontline of PHP cyber-security scramble

sentences.text: But also highlight how misinformation and panic has made things a lot worse.
sentences.article_title: 'It's been relentless' say IT workers on frontline of PHP cyber-security scramble

sentences.text: "It's been relentless," says UK-based system administrator Adam Mudd.
sentences.article_title: 'It's been relentless' say IT workers on frontline of PHP cyber-security scramble

sentences.text: He said he had never had so many messages from people who were worried about their websites.
sentences.article_title: 'It's been relentless' say IT workers on frontline of PHP cyber-security scramble

sentences.text: "The biggest challenge has been juggling clients who want their sites taken offline as a precaution, while trying to coordinate updates and fixes across countless different setups," he said.
sentences.article_title: 'It's been relentless' say IT workers on frontline of PHP cyber-security scramble

sentences.text: "Sometimes it takes me longer to take a website down than to fix the PHP problem." PHP is a very popular programming language which powers millions of websites.
sentences.article_title: 'It's been relentless' say IT workers on frontline of PHP cyber-security scramble

sentences.text: But two critical flaws were found with the system that led to the emergency response, with national cyber-security authorities urging IT teams to download a security fix urgently or take websites and servers offline.
sentences.article_title: 'It's been relentless' say IT workers on frontline of PHP cyber-security scramble

sentences.text: Mudd says since then he has been under enormous pressure and has lost a huge amount of sleep - working early and not finishing until 22:30 BST to secure his customers' systems.
sentences.article_title: 'It's been relentless' say IT workers on frontline of PHP cyber-security scramble

sentences.text: In Mauritius, IT administrator Loganaden Velvindron said he too was flat out since his team realised just how much software relies on PHP.
sentences.article_title: 'It's been relentless' say IT workers on frontline of PHP cyber-security scramble

sentences.text: "Many versions of php running are completely end-of-life, so we are having to rebuilding web apps and change code in some cases," he said.
sentences.article_title: 'It's been relentless' say IT workers on frontline of PHP cyber-security scramble

sentences.text: He said part of the problem was the announcement about the security vulnerabilities in PHP came as a surprise, without much time to prepare for action.
sentences.article_title: 'It's been relentless' say IT workers on frontline of PHP cyber-security scramble

sentences.text: Jon Jones, Technical director for a digital advertising company, was also spurred into action by the alerts.
sentences.article_title: 'It's been relentless' say IT workers on frontline of PHP cyber-security scramble

sentences.text: "Seeing the warning drop was definitely eye-opening and a new experience we've not dealt with before," he said.
sentences.article_title: 'It's been relentless' say IT workers on frontline of PHP cyber-security scramble

sentences.text: "But, in a way, it was exciting feeling like a bit of a Hollywood action scene." The PHP Foundation, which manages the programming language, released its software fix and there was a scramble for people to download it.
sentences.article_title: 'It's been relentless' say IT workers on frontline of PHP cyber-security scramble

sentences.text: Jones said it felt like "the race was on" when the patch launched at 15:00 BST on Wednesday.
sentences.article_title: 'It's been relentless' say IT workers on frontline of PHP cyber-security scramble

sentences.text: "It was also a bit nerve-racking as anyone who has applied software updates before would know, there's always a chance than an update can cause other issues," he said.
sentences.article_title: 'It's been relentless' say IT workers on frontline of PHP cyber-security scramble

sentences.text: The rush came as someone had leaked details of the PHP flaw early - and it was heavily rumoured that cyber-criminals were already trying to carry out attacks.
sentences.article_title: 'It's been relentless' say IT workers on frontline of PHP cyber-security scramble

sentences.text: But cyber experts are also now questioning whether or not those rumours were real.
sentences.article_title: 'It's been relentless' say IT workers on frontline of PHP cyber-security scramble

sentences.text: "We were flooded with rubbish intel about hackers being out there actively with working Proof of Concept (PoC) methods," said UK cyber expert Daniel Card.
sentences.article_title: 'It's been relentless' say IT workers on frontline of PHP cyber-security scramble

sentences.text: He said he also been flat out since Tuesday when the rumours of PHP hacks began circulating.
sentences.article_title: 'It's been relentless' say IT workers on frontline of PHP cyber-security scramble

sentences.text: "This isn't the first time we've had a situation like this but it feels like it's been on another dimension," he said.
sentences.article_title: 'It's been relentless' say IT workers on frontline of PHP cyber-security scramble

sentences.text: He agreed that on paper the PHP vulnerabilities were very serious and should be taken seriously, but he and many others are frustrated with the misinformation about hackers being on the loose.
sentences.article_title: 'It's been relentless' say IT workers on frontline of PHP cyber-security scramble

sentences.text: As well as the alerts from government agencies - even the Prime Minister of Japan - cyber-security companies also made errors which didn't help.
sentences.article_title: 'It's been relentless' say IT workers on frontline of PHP cyber-security scramble

sentences.text: One major firm in this space issued warnings saying hackers had a working PoC - only to have to retract it.
sentences.article_title: 'It's been relentless' say IT workers on frontline of PHP cyber-security scramble

sentences.text: In spite of warnings from Cloudflare and AWS that "millions of hacking attempts" had been made every hour, there is also no evidence of large scale data breaches or cyber-attacks.
sentences.article_title: 'It's been relentless' say IT workers on frontline of PHP cyber-security scramble

sentences.text: It is true that hackers have been seen to use AI to attempt to build attack methods, but none of them seem to be working at scale at the moment - something that may well change soon.
sentences.article_title: 'It's been relentless' say IT workers on frontline of PHP cyber-security scramble

sentences.text: AI was also used to find the PHP flaws which had been hidden from human researchers for decades.
sentences.article_title: 'It's been relentless' say IT workers on frontline of PHP cyber-security scramble

sentences.text: The IT workers we spoke to all agreed that these kinds of serious flaws were going to be uncovered more frequently now that AI tools had become so good at hacking.
sentences.article_title: 'It's been relentless' say IT workers on frontline of PHP cyber-security scramble

sentences.text: But some in the industry are concerned about how people were told about the critical vulnerabilities in PHP, as they fear improvements in AI will throw up more incidents like it.
sentences.article_title: 'It's been relentless' say IT workers on frontline of PHP cyber-security scramble

sentences.text: "We're going to find scary vulnerabilities with the amazing capabilities that OpenAI and Anthropic are bringing online, but we need to calibrate the messaging," posted Mark Maunder, founder of Wordfence - a Wordpress security tool.
sentences.article_title: 'It's been relentless' say IT workers on frontline of PHP cyber-security scramble

sentences.text: He said there was a risk of "alert fatigue" which could be a big problem if a fully exploitable and serious vulnerability arose.

sentences.text: I once worked opposite a site where a shopping centre was being built.
sentences.article_title: Zoe Kleinman: PHP is the cyber equivalent of an unexploded bomb

sentences.text: We were warned there might be unexploded bombs from World War Two unearthed during the construction.
sentences.article_title: Zoe Kleinman: PHP is the cyber equivalent of an unexploded bomb

sentences.text: In the end, there were none, but procedures were put in place as a precaution and we all had to practice filing into designated safe zones inside our building.
sentences.article_title: Zoe Kleinman: PHP is the cyber equivalent of an unexploded bomb

sentences.text: The PHP story feels like the cyber equivalent of an unexploded bomb - I have never seen such a dramatic, public and global response to a cyber event that hasn't happened yet.
sentences.article_title: Zoe Kleinman: PHP is the cyber equivalent of an unexploded bomb

sentences.text: There has been no painful attack like the ransomware we saw knock out M&S and JLR in 2025.
sentences.article_title: Zoe Kleinman: PHP is the cyber equivalent of an unexploded bomb

sentences.text: But the potential threat is so serious that websites around the world have been taken down as a precaution.
sentences.article_title: Zoe Kleinman: PHP is the cyber equivalent of an unexploded bomb

sentences.text: Less than two months ago , 100 tech companies wrote an open letter warning the world to adopt a new level of cyber resilience in the age of AI.
sentences.article_title: Zoe Kleinman: PHP is the cyber equivalent of an unexploded bomb

sentences.text: It turns out we didn't have to wait very long to find out what they meant.
sentences.article_title: Zoe Kleinman: PHP is the cyber equivalent of an unexploded bomb

sentences.text: The weaknesses found in the PHP programming language, which is used by millions of websites, had been quietly resting there for years and are not easy to exploit.
sentences.article_title: Zoe Kleinman: PHP is the cyber equivalent of an unexploded bomb

sentences.text: One cyber security researcher told me he'd been up all night trying to do it as an experiment, but it was proving very difficult.
sentences.article_title: Zoe Kleinman: PHP is the cyber equivalent of an unexploded bomb

sentences.text: However, things that are very difficult for humans are increasingly very little trouble for AI.
sentences.article_title: Zoe Kleinman: PHP is the cyber equivalent of an unexploded bomb

sentences.text: The tech is getting a lot of credit here for assisting researchers in finding the bugs, and the PHP foundation, which oversees the programming language, was on the case and issued a fix.
sentences.article_title: Zoe Kleinman: PHP is the cyber equivalent of an unexploded bomb

sentences.text: It was supposed to be kept quiet until everyone had a chance to fix their sites - but the news was leaked.
sentences.article_title: Zoe Kleinman: PHP is the cyber equivalent of an unexploded bomb

sentences.text: From that point the clock started ticking.
sentences.article_title: Zoe Kleinman: PHP is the cyber equivalent of an unexploded bomb

sentences.text: As I write this, there are no reports that anyone or anything has succeeded in using the flaws to attack a site.
sentences.article_title: Zoe Kleinman: PHP is the cyber equivalent of an unexploded bomb

sentences.text: "There's a real dilemma," said Prof Alan Woodward from Surrey University.
sentences.article_title: Zoe Kleinman: PHP is the cyber equivalent of an unexploded bomb

sentences.text: "How do you alert people they need to be ready, and then that a patch is urgently required, whilst not alerting attackers?
sentences.article_title: Zoe Kleinman: PHP is the cyber equivalent of an unexploded bomb

sentences.text: "Basically you're telling everyone about the problem at the same time and hoping the defenders aren't awake enough to act as soon as the patch is out." But we do know from large web companies like Cloudflare and Palo Alto Networks that millions of attempts have been made.
sentences.article_title: Zoe Kleinman: PHP is the cyber equivalent of an unexploded bomb

sentences.text: We probably won't know for a while whether it has worked for any criminals, because the companies affected might not be aware yet either.
sentences.article_title: Zoe Kleinman: PHP is the cyber equivalent of an unexploded bomb

sentences.text: As far as we know the unexploded bomb remains intact for now, and for some experts this is a success.
sentences.article_title: Zoe Kleinman: PHP is the cyber equivalent of an unexploded bomb

sentences.text: Gina Neff, Professor of Responsible AI at Queen Mary University, described this as a good news story.
sentences.article_title: Zoe Kleinman: PHP is the cyber equivalent of an unexploded bomb

sentences.text: "We've seen how a team of people supported by the large AI company have used AI to find the problem, work for months together to solve it and get everybody ready to be safe and secure," she told the Today Programme on BBC Radio 4.
sentences.article_title: Zoe Kleinman: PHP is the cyber equivalent of an unexploded bomb

sentences.text: "We have enormous capability to handle these risks." But the baddies can use AI too, and those same tools are probably churning away right now trying to get in.
sentences.article_title: Zoe Kleinman: PHP is the cyber equivalent of an unexploded bomb

sentences.text: Organisations and businesses are still scrambling to update their systems after cyber-security flaws were revealed in a widely-used programming language, PHP.
sentences.article_title: Race to update services' computer systems after cyber-security flaw found

sentences.text: Websites around the world were taken offline on Wednesday and Thursday after the developers of PHP said "critical vulnerabilities" were found in the back-end language, used in web development for decades.
sentences.article_title: Race to update services' computer systems after cyber-security flaw found

sentences.text: Researchers warned the "severe" flaws could expose millions of sites using it to potential hacks if left unpatched - and the UK government was among those to take some sites offline as a precaution.
sentences.article_title: Race to update services' computer systems after cyber-security flaw found

sentences.text: There have been no successful attacks reported so far, but experts say any impact may take time - even months - to become fully apparent.
sentences.article_title: Race to update services' computer systems after cyber-security flaw found

sentences.text: Downing Street said on Thursday "some" limited government services "may be offline" while security work was being carried out.
sentences.article_title: Race to update services' computer systems after cyber-security flaw found

sentences.text: "The information I have is that 32 Government services are unavailable and four are partially unavailable," tech minister Baroness Lloyd of Effra told the House of Lords.
sentences.article_title: Race to update services' computer systems after cyber-security flaw found

sentences.text: She attributed this to having "largely resulted from precautionary measures taken to protect systems while security updates and mitigations are applied".
sentences.article_title: Race to update services' computer systems after cyber-security flaw found

sentences.text: The government did not specify which services were taken offline - but it said no large UK public-facing critical services had been affected.
sentences.article_title: Race to update services' computer systems after cyber-security flaw found

sentences.text: A spokesperson said work had already taken place across government to "identify and fix potential exposures to our systems and our experts are continuing to work closely with both OpenAI and international partners on this issue".
sentences.article_title: Race to update services' computer systems after cyber-security flaw found

sentences.text: "But this does not mean they were hacked, and work continues to resolve any issues," they added.
sentences.article_title: Race to update services' computer systems after cyber-security flaw found

sentences.text: Olly Whitehouse, chief technology officer of the National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC), called the event "unprecedented".
sentences.article_title: Race to update services' computer systems after cyber-security flaw found

sentences.text: "It will be universally felt, I suspect," he told BBC Radio 4's World At One.
sentences.article_title: Race to update services' computer systems after cyber-security flaw found

sentences.text: But he said there were "no indications" of any successful breaches by hackers.
sentences.article_title: Race to update services' computer systems after cyber-security flaw found

sentences.text: He said the NCSC was "starting to see positive confirmation" that advice sent to those affected , external had been received and was being acted on.
sentences.article_title: Race to update services' computer systems after cyber-security flaw found

sentences.text: "Hacking has been around for many years," he said.
sentences.article_title: Race to update services' computer systems after cyber-security flaw found

sentences.text: "The government are the ones who set the rules for other organisations... they just need to effectively be practising what they're preaching at this point." Dean Presley, who has a garage in Chepstow, South Wales, told BBC Your Voice he had been unable to properly process MOTs online.
sentences.article_title: Race to update services' computer systems after cyber-security flaw found

sentences.article_title: Race to update services' computer systems after cyber-security flaw found

sentences.text: PHP stands for PHP: Hypertext Preprocessor.
sentences.article_title: Race to update services' computer systems after cyber-security flaw found

sentences.text: It's a programming language which runs on a web server, behind the scenes of a website, and effectively lets you see the sites you visit.
sentences.article_title: Race to update services' computer systems after cyber-security flaw found

sentences.text: When you go to a site, PHP is the code which collects data and effectively turns it into a page you can read.
sentences.article_title: Race to update services' computer systems after cyber-security flaw found

sentences.text: It was developed in the early 1990s to help serve dynamic web pages and applications, but still powers lots of platforms today.
sentences.article_title: Race to update services' computer systems after cyber-security flaw found

sentences.text: PHP has been used across a wide range of platforms including Wikipedia, online shops and WordPress – the system behind many websites - as well as to write tools to build web apps, with Laravel, Symfony and Drupal among popular PHP frameworks.
sentences.article_title: Race to update services' computer systems after cyber-security flaw found

sentences.text: According to cyber-security firm Wiz , external , which helped uncover the critical PHP vulnerabilities surfaced this week, PHP powers 70% of the world's websites.
sentences.article_title: Race to update services' computer systems after cyber-security flaw found

sentences.text: And it said the flaws - now coined "php2shell" - were inherent in the language itself, affecting many past versions of it.
sentences.article_title: Race to update services' computer systems after cyber-security flaw found

sentences.text: The PHP Foundation, the non-profit which maintains the programming language, warned this meant that, under the right conditions, an unauthenticated attacker would be able to remotely execute code on servers running PHP.
sentences.article_title: Race to update services' computer systems after cyber-security flaw found

sentences.text: Some large organisations said they had seen a high volume of attempts to breach their systems.
sentences.article_title: Race to update services' computer systems after cyber-security flaw found

sentences.text: Matthew Prince, the boss of internet infrastructure firm Cloudflare, wrote on X , external on Thursday that the company saw "thousands" of attempts to exploit the PHP vulnerabilities across its network in the 10 hours before it was publicly announced.
sentences.article_title: Race to update services' computer systems after cyber-security flaw found

sentences.text: "That jumped to tens of thousands in the 45 minutes post announcement, hundreds of thousands within two hours, and millions now," he added.
sentences.article_title: Race to update services' computer systems after cyber-security flaw found

sentences.text: Amazon also says it saw hackers attempt to exploit the flaws, but its websites were operating as normal.
sentences.article_title: Race to update services' computer systems after cyber-security flaw found

sentences.text: Cyber researchers at Calif and Wiz unearthed the php2shell flaw, theorised by the PHP Foundation in 2024, in part using OpenAI tools While the impact of the PHP flaw remains to be seen, disruption continued for businesses and organisations after many sites were taken down on Wednesday.
sentences.article_title: Race to update services' computer systems after cyber-security flaw found

sentences.text: The website of a Dutch agency specialising in cyber-security, Finland's government and parts of Wikipedia, taken temporarily offline, had returned to business as usual by Thursday.
sentences.article_title: Race to update services' computer systems after cyber-security flaw found

sentences.text: But a number of sites appeared to have been taken offline on Thursday, as operators rushed to check if PHP might be running within their systems or if any patches were required.
sentences.article_title: Race to update services' computer systems after cyber-security flaw found

sentences.text: In France, telecommunications company Orange also said , external it had suspended access to certain services globally while it deployed security fixes.
sentences.article_title: Race to update services' computer systems after cyber-security flaw found

sentences.text: According to some cyber-security researchers using scans to check servers at risk of the PHP vulnerability, the rate of organisations implementing patches - but not as quickly as might be hoped globally.
sentences.article_title: Race to update services' computer systems after cyber-security flaw found

sentences.text: "The window to respond has shrunk dramatically," said Matt Hull, VP of cyber intelligence and response at global cyber security company NCC Group.
sentences.article_title: Race to update services' computer systems after cyber-security flaw found

sentences.text: "A few years ago, attackers might have taken weeks to exploit a vulnerability.
sentences.article_title: Race to update services' computer systems after cyber-security flaw found

sentences.text: Now, it can be days or hours." Hull also highlighted the extent of the task facing developers and engineers working to deal with the issue.
sentences.article_title: Race to update services' computer systems after cyber-security flaw found

sentences.text: "Several days into this incident, security professionals might already be dealing with significant burnout," he said, urging a need to "make time to rest, share the workload and look after each other".
sentences.article_title: Race to update services' computer systems after cyber-security flaw found

sentences.text: Governments and some of the world's biggest companies are rushing to protect systems that use PHP before hackers can exploit the flaws.

sentences.article_title: UK working to identify exposure after global cyber-security warning

sentences.article_title: UK working to identify exposure after global cyber-security warning

sentences.text: As well as the scale of the flaw, Woodward said the nature of it means "an attacker can get their own code on to the webserver and run it and basically do whatever they like." "They can steal data , they can go to other parts of your network.
sentences.article_title: UK working to identify exposure after global cyber-security warning

sentences.text: All sort of things like that - even plant a backdoor to get in later on, so it's pretty serious," Woodward told BBC Radio 4's Today programme.

sentences.article_title: UK working to identify exposure after global cyber-security warning

sentences.text: The attacks occurred after the leak, but before the embargo was lifted on the PHP warning.
sentences.article_title: UK working to identify exposure after global cyber-security warning

sentences.text: The use of AI means that "more actors can act within hours or even minutes once technical details of a vulnerability are disclosed", Moses added.

sentences.text: She warned that threats would only become more commonplace as AI technology rapidly improves.

sentences.text: Earlier this month, the US announced it would suspend eight technology firms , including Microsoft, India's Infosys, Tata Consultancy Services, Wipro and HCL Technologies, from hiring skilled international workers on a permanent basis through a widely used visa pathway.
sentences.article_title: Trump's green card curbs test Indian tech workers' American dream

sentences.text: New and pending applications under the Permanent Labor Certification Program, or PERM, have been frozen.
sentences.article_title: Trump's green card curbs test Indian tech workers' American dream

sentences.text: This is a big blow to Indians who hold a majority of H-1B visas - a temporary visa for specialists - which they used to work in the US while relying on PERM to get a green card and, ultimately, citizenship.
sentences.article_title: Trump's green card curbs test Indian tech workers' American dream

sentences.text: The latest announcement is in line with Trump's push for stricter skilled-worker immigration rules, which tech firms have been adapting to and, therefore, the impact on businesses may be minimal, experts say.
sentences.article_title: Trump's green card curbs test Indian tech workers' American dream

sentences.text: Nasscom, the trade association of India's $300bn (£226bn) technology industry, says that Indian companies have reduced the dependence on H-1B visas and are hiring more locally.
sentences.article_title: Trump's green card curbs test Indian tech workers' American dream

sentences.text: "Consequently, the number of employees transitioning from H-1B visas to permanent residency through the PERM process is also relatively limited," the association adds.
sentences.article_title: Trump's green card curbs test Indian tech workers' American dream

sentences.text: Wipro said in a statement that more than 80% of its workforce in the US is locally hired.
sentences.article_title: Trump's green card curbs test Indian tech workers' American dream

sentences.text: Tata Consultancy Services (TCS), said its PERM applications were in single digits in the last two years.

sentences.text: African diaspora is finding new audiences in a city celebrated for its musical heritage A new sound is taking Bristol's dancefloors by storm.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: Driven by rolling log drums, syncopated rhythms and infectious melodies, amapiano and other electronic sounds from across the African diaspora are finding new audiences in a city celebrated for its musical heritage.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: Behind these parties is a new generation of black promoters passionate about creating spaces where black people can hear their music, celebrate their cultures and feel like they belong.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: But for some, building these spaces has also meant confronting the familiar challenge of finding spaces where black music and the communities around it are welcomed and not feared.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: Unkle Mykel started hosting events to connect to different cultures Bristol-based promoter Unkle Mykel's journey into events began in his own back garden after he moved to Bristol in 2017.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: What started as garden barbecues gradually grew into a way of bringing people together, particularly members of Bristol's black, Asian and minority ethnic communities.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: "It's about celebrating our cultures, bringing people into that fold and connecting," says the 32-year-old, who hosts Bristol Barbecue Family and The Aux Social.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: Originally from Kenya, Mykel moved to the UK in 2005.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: Since then, he has witnessed changes in the visibility of African music.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: "There was no Afrobeats on the airwaves," he laughs, recalling his early years in the country, when he says Caribbean reggae, dancehall and soca were more prominent in the musical landscape he encountered.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: Now, he sees the growing popularity of genres such as amapiano - a popular South African house music subgenre - as an opportunity to broaden the scene.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: "We don't need to pretend to be nobody else, we're just us.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: It just took a while to get there." DJ and promoter Khiah Lou runs amapiano event called Khaya Nights For 30-year-old DJ and promoter Khiah Lou, representation, she says, is central to her work.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: Last year she launched Khaya Nights, an event dedicated to amapiano and other African Caribbean electronic dance music.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: Having performed internationally, she had seen how other cities had developed a wider range of events celebrating these sounds.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: Bristol, she felt, was lagging behind.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: Rather than wait for the scene to develop, Khiah decided to help build it herself.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: "If we don't do it, who else is going to do it?" she says.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: "Young black people are starting to make a way for themselves because I don't think we have a choice." Khiah says these nights provide a place where people can connect with their identities and see their cultures reflected in the city around them.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: "At first it seems like it's just a party, but it's so much more than that," she says.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: "It's really important for your own self-identity.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: If your community doesn't have events, where do you feel you can go?" "At first it seems like just a party, but it's so much more than that,' says Khiah Tazmin Samuels, who DJs as Azumei, shares those concerns about representation.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: As part of Rushtown, a black-led music collective, Tazmin wants to champion sounds and subcultures from across Africa, Latin America and the Caribbean.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: "My main motivation for getting together with people and starting Rushtown came from seeing the lack of representation of black music that black people are currently listening to within the city," says Tazmin.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: She sees encouraging signs, with more black music-focused brands emerging in Bristol.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: But she believes the wider music industry has yet to recognise the value of what these promoters are building.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: Tazmin says the wider music industry must recognise the value of black promoters But creating these spaces is not always straightforward.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: Khiah says she has struggled to find venues willing to host nights aimed at black audiences.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: Although she considers Bristol an inclusive city, her experience as a promoter has revealed a different side of its nightlife.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: "I've had some venue owners straight up tell me they're worried about having a black event," she says.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: "I feel like black crowds are kind of met with fear, and that's really disheartening." Mykel describes similar tensions, saying that some venues are enthusiastic about hosting his events, only to face objections from people in the surrounding community.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: The Bamboo Club opened in 1966 as a social hub for Bristol's Caribbean community The young promoters' experiences echo a much longer history of black Bristolians having to create their own spaces for music and social life.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: Many black people were turned away from existing clubs and bars in Bristol during the 1960s, which led to the creation of  "blues parties", un-licensed house parties where people danced to genres such as ska, reggae and rocksteady.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: In 1966, Tony Bullimore and his Jamaican-born wife Lalel, opened the Bamboo Club, which served as a cultural lifeline for the city's Caribbean community.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: Glen Crooks, 70, who used to perform at the Bamboo Club when he was younger, remembers "sneaking in" with his friends when they were young.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: "It was the only place that we could have," he recalls.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: "Especially all the Caribbean people could go and really have a good time." Rushtown aims to champion a variety of music genres from the African diaspora Marti Burgess, who has been a co-owner of the nightclub Lakota since 1994, says although attitudes have changed over the years, some prejudices remain.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: "There is a long history of treating a predominantly black audience as a concern, rather than recognising the audience, creativity and business that a promoter is bringing," she says.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: "They should not have to keep proving that black audiences are welcome or commercially worthwhile." Growing up, Marti was surrounded by music.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: Her parents went to the blues clubs and attended the Bamboo Club when it hosted artists such as Bob Marley, Desmond Dekker and Johnny Nash.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: "It was through listening to the adults' conversations that I came to understand how much those spaces had grown out of exclusion from mainstream venues," she says.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: "Latino Fest this summer opened our eyes further to the audiences and musical communities we could welcome," says Marti.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: "We want people across the different genres of black music to see Lakota as a venue that is open to them, where they can bring their music and their audiences." Follow BBC Bristol on Facebook , external , X , external and Instagram , external .

sentences.text: Blackpool is one of four shortlisted locations to be the next UK City of Culture Blackpool, Milton Keynes, Sheffield and Wrexham have been shortlisted to become the UK's City of Culture in 2029.
sentences.article_title: Four locations in the running to be UK City of Culture 2029

sentences.text: The winning location will be announced in May and will be the fifth holder of the title - following Derry-Londonderry, Hull, Coventry and Bradford.

sentences.text: A different location is given the City of Culture title every four years.
sentences.article_title: Four locations in the running to be UK City of Culture 2029

sentences.article_title: Four locations in the running to be UK City of Culture 2029

sentences.article_title: Morocco's first female prime minister caught between the king, clerics, and feminists

sentences.text: Some of the country's most contentious debates over gender equality centre on family law, including inheritance, marriage and divorce.
sentences.article_title: Morocco's first female prime minister caught between the king, clerics, and feminists

sentences.text: Under existing inheritance rules, a daughter typically receives half the share of a son in comparable circumstances.
sentences.article_title: Morocco's first female prime minister caught between the king, clerics, and feminists

sentences.text: The Higher Council of Ulemas, the country's body of religious scholars, has resisted calls for equal inheritance, citing Islamic jurisprudence.
sentences.article_title: Morocco's first female prime minister caught between the king, clerics, and feminists

sentences.text: It has also rejected proposals to abolish taasib, a rule that can require female orphans without brothers to share their inheritance with male relatives, including distant ones.
sentences.article_title: Morocco's first female prime minister caught between the king, clerics, and feminists

sentences.text: In a 2022 report, Morocco's National Human Rights Council said unequal inheritance rules contributed to poverty among women.
sentences.article_title: Morocco's first female prime minister caught between the king, clerics, and feminists

sentences.text: Polygamy is also legal under certain conditions.
sentences.article_title: Morocco's first female prime minister caught between the king, clerics, and feminists

sentences.text: Proposed changes to the family code have included allowing women to stipulate in their marriage contracts that their husbands cannot take another wife.
sentences.article_title: Morocco's first female prime minister caught between the king, clerics, and feminists

sentences.text: But exceptions remain, including provisions relating to a first wife's infertility or illness, which women's rights groups have criticised on grounds of privacy and medical confidentiality.
sentences.article_title: Morocco's first female prime minister caught between the king, clerics, and feminists

sentences.text: These issues are at the heart of proposals to reform the Moudawana, Morocco's family code, which governs marriage, divorce and child custody.
sentences.article_title: Morocco's first female prime minister caught between the king, clerics, and feminists

sentences.text: A package of changes was announced in 2024, but the reforms have yet to become law.
sentences.article_title: Morocco's first female prime minister caught between the king, clerics, and feminists

sentences.text: As well as family law, some young women hope the new prime minister will try to improve education for girls.
sentences.article_title: Morocco's first female prime minister caught between the king, clerics, and feminists

sentences.text: Morocco's High Commission for Planning, the country's official national statistics agency, found in 2025 that just 55% of girls aged 15–17 were going to school in rural areas, where poverty, early marriage and dropping out of school remain key barriers.
sentences.article_title: Morocco's first female prime minister caught between the king, clerics, and feminists

sentences.text: In urban areas, it was 100%.
sentences.article_title: Morocco's first female prime minister caught between the king, clerics, and feminists

sentences.text: "Many girls in rural Morocco drop out of school early because schools are far away, transport is unsafe or unavailable, and families with limited means often keep their daughters at home," Chifae Laazouzi, a young Moroccan woman, tells the BBC.
sentences.article_title: Morocco's first female prime minister caught between the king, clerics, and feminists

sentences.text: She says one reason is that many girls in poor and rural areas cannot afford menstrual sanitary products.
sentences.article_title: Morocco's first female prime minister caught between the king, clerics, and feminists

sentences.text: "Menstrual health is still treated as a taboo...
sentences.article_title: Morocco's first female prime minister caught between the king, clerics, and feminists

sentences.text: I would like to see free menstrual products in schools," Laazouzi says.
sentences.article_title: Morocco's first female prime minister caught between the king, clerics, and feminists

sentences.text: El Mansouri is no newcomer to politics.
sentences.article_title: Morocco's first female prime minister caught between the king, clerics, and feminists

sentences.text: Over more than two decades in public life, she has served as mayor of Marrakech, held government posts and sat in parliament.
sentences.article_title: Morocco's first female prime minister caught between the king, clerics, and feminists

sentences.text: For the past five years, she served as minister for national territory planning, urban planning, housing and city policy under the previous Prime Minister Aziz Akhannouch.
sentences.article_title: Morocco's first female prime minister caught between the king, clerics, and feminists

sentences.text: After her appointment, El Mansouri presented the moment as a milestone for Moroccan women.
sentences.article_title: Morocco's first female prime minister caught between the king, clerics, and feminists

sentences.text: "Being the first female head of government is not just a source of pride for me, but for all the women of the kingdom," she said.
sentences.article_title: Morocco's first female prime minister caught between the king, clerics, and feminists

sentences.text: Since her appointment, she has not indicated whether she plans to try and push through the reforms to the family code.
sentences.article_title: Morocco's first female prime minister caught between the king, clerics, and feminists

sentences.text: In her political career so far, she has not made any prominent public statements about women's rights, even while changes to inheritance rules, polygamy and the family code were being widely debated.
sentences.article_title: Morocco's first female prime minister caught between the king, clerics, and feminists

sentences.text: "Two headlines have dominated coverage of [September's] parliamentary election in Morocco: a two-decade low turnout and King Mohammed VI's appointment of a woman as prime minister for the first time in this country's history," she tells the BBC.
sentences.article_title: Morocco's first female prime minister caught between the king, clerics, and feminists

sentences.text: "The latter cannot be understood without the former." Official figures put turnout at just 38% of registered voters, while the proportion of all eligible voters who cast a ballot was even lower.
sentences.article_title: Morocco's first female prime minister caught between the king, clerics, and feminists

sentences.text: Fernandez-Molina describes the appointment as an example of "authoritarian state feminism, a top-down, selective instrumentalisation of the struggle for women's rights for regime legitimation purposes".
sentences.article_title: Morocco's first female prime minister caught between the king, clerics, and feminists

sentences.text: She argues that promoting a woman to the highest government office might be intended to project an image of modernisation and progress, even when the political system and the pace of social reform remain largely unchanged.
sentences.article_title: Morocco's first female prime minister caught between the king, clerics, and feminists

sentences.text: For Moroccan women's rights advocate Yasmina Benslimane, the appointment breaks a longstanding barrier, but says El Mansouri's background is also important.
sentences.article_title: Morocco's first female prime minister caught between the king, clerics, and feminists

sentences.text: "It does challenge stereotypes, because it finally breaks a ceiling that was never broken," she says.
sentences.article_title: Morocco's first female prime minister caught between the king, clerics, and feminists

sentences.text: "But it matters how she got there." El Mansouri's late father was a pasha, a senior local official, and a diplomat.
sentences.article_title: Morocco's first female prime minister caught between the king, clerics, and feminists

sentences.text: Benslimane argues that her privileged background and access to political networks distinguish her from many Moroccan women who have fewer opportunities to enter public life.
sentences.article_title: Morocco's first female prime minister caught between the king, clerics, and feminists

sentences.text: For Benslimane, like many women's rights groups in the country, reform of the Moudawana remains a key test of the new government.
sentences.article_title: Morocco's first female prime minister caught between the king, clerics, and feminists

sentences.text: However, El Mansouri's room for manoeuvre is shaped by the country's political system.
sentences.article_title: Morocco's first female prime minister caught between the king, clerics, and feminists

sentences.text: The king retains extensive powers over key areas, including defence and foreign affairs, while the head of government operates within a system where authority is shared.
sentences.article_title: Morocco's first female prime minister caught between the king, clerics, and feminists

sentences.text: When it comes to Moudawana reform, she would have to face the country's religious scholars, who are mostly men.
sentences.article_title: Morocco's first female prime minister caught between the king, clerics, and feminists

sentences.text: While some Moroccan women welcome her appointment, they say it is what she does as prime minister that really counts.
sentences.article_title: Morocco's first female prime minister caught between the king, clerics, and feminists

sentences.text: "I don't think El Mansouri should be judged by the fact that she is a woman.
sentences.article_title: Morocco's first female prime minister caught between the king, clerics, and feminists

sentences.text: Being a woman in power doesn't automatically make someone a champion of women's rights," Sara Zouiten, a young Moroccan woman, tells the BBC.
